effect_or_estimate: No statistical or meaningful differences in punching force, pacing or RPE between conditions (P > 0.05; differences <= 2%)
limitations: n=15, male, simulated bout on a punch integrator (84 maximal punches over three rounds), not live competition. A null with modest n cannot rule out small effects.
citation: Halperin I, Chapman DW, Thompson KG, Abbiss C. False-performance feedback does not affect punching forces and pacing of elite boxers. J Sports Sci. 2018.
ppbf_implication: GOVERNANCE ANCHOR: SHADOW must never manipulate feedback content to influence an athlete, and this study indicates it would not work in elite boxers anyway. Feedback surfaced by PPBF must be truthful and traceable to the underlying observation.
verified_title: False-performance feedback does not affect punching forces and pacing of elite boxers.

track: Track 1 - Motor Learning & Skill Acquisition
topic: Skill level moderation of cue type
claim: External-focus instructions improved kicking performance only among LESS skilled youth competitors in a combat sport, indicating cue effectiveness may depend on skill level in young athletes.
effect_or_estimate: Improved kicking performance with external versus internal focus instructions only among the less skilled participants
boxing_specific: PARTIAL - taekwondo, a striking combat sport, not boxing
limitations: Small n per cell; acute performance not learning; sits in tension with the Chua et al. meta-regression finding that skill level did not moderate (A1-005).
citation: Siltanen S, Bottas R. Instructions for External Focus of Attention Improved Taekwondo Kicking Performance Only Among Less Skilled Youth. Percept Mot Skills. 2022;129.
ppbf_implication: The cue library must carry an athlete_level field, and PPBF should test whether cue effectiveness differs by level in its own athletes rather than assuming one cue set fits all.
verified_title: Instructions for External Focus of Attention Improved Taekwondo Kicking Performance Only Among Less Skilled Youth.

track: Track 1 - Motor Learning & Skill Acquisition
claim: Head trauma in boxing has been systematically reviewed and meta-analysed, and international concussion consensus (6th Concussion in Sport Group, Amsterdam 2022) governs assessment and return-to-play decisions.
population: Boxers (amateur and professional); athletes generally for the consensus statement
study_design: Systematic review with meta-analysis; international consensus statement
effect_or_estimate: No effect estimate carried here - clinical decisions are outside SHADOW scope by design
boxing_specific: PARTIAL - boxing-specific for the head-trauma review; general sport for the consensus statement
limitations: An older systematic review of amateur boxing and chronic traumatic brain injury described the observational evidence base as limited in quality; this remains an evolving clinical field with jurisdictional differences in rules and medical oversight.
citation: Donnelly RR, Ugbolue UC, Gao Y, et al. A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Investigating Head Trauma in Boxing. Clin J Sport Med. 2023; Patricios JS, Schneider KJ, Dvorak J, et al. Consensus statement on concussion in sport: the 6th International Conference on Concussion in Sport - Amsterdam, October 2022. Br J Sports Med. 2023; Loosemore M, Knowles CH, Whyte GP. Amateur boxing and risk of chronic traumatic brain injury: systematic review of observational studies. BMJ. 2007.
ppbf_implication: HARD BOUNDARY. SHADOW performs NO concussion assessment, NO return-to-play clearance and NO contact/sparring medical clearance. Those decisions are owned by a qualified physician or licensed medical officer under the relevant governing body, with the head coach and safeguarding lead executing the resulting restriction. SHADOW's only role is to surface the restriction status a human has set (pilot.shadow_medical_administrative_status) and block conflicting training assignments.
verified_title: Amateur boxing and risk of chronic traumatic brain injury: systematic review of observational studies.

track: Track 1 - Motor Learning & Skill Acquisition
claim: A systematic review of 52 randomised controlled trials of golf motor learning shows the density of RCT evidence available in a single closed-skill sport - and by contrast the near-absence of comparable boxing trials.
effect_or_estimate: Studies grouped by cognitive training, practice scheduling, augmented feedback, implicit and explicit learning, and focus of attention
boxing_specific: No - golf; cited here as a contrast case
limitations: Golf is a self-paced closed skill; boxing is an open, reactive, contested skill. The golf evidence base does not transfer.
citation: Barzyk P, Gruber M. Motor learning in golf - a systematic review. Front Sports Act Living. 2024;6:1324615.
ppbf_implication: Quantifies the gap: 52 RCTs exist for golf motor learning; this search located no comparable RCT set for boxing skill acquisition. PPBF's own pilot data would be a genuine contribution, not a duplication.
verified_title: Motor learning in golf-a systematic review.

track: Track 1 - Motor Learning & Skill Acquisition
claim: No randomised controlled trial of a boxing skill-acquisition instructional method (cue type, practice schedule or feedback schedule) with a delayed retention and transfer test was located in this search.
study_design: Absence of evidence following structured search of PubMed, OpenAlex and Crossref
effect_or_estimate: No estimate exists
transfer_status: N/A - nothing to transfer from within boxing
limitations: Absence of evidence in this search is not proof of absence; non-English, thesis and federation-internal literature was not exhaustively covered, and OpenAlex querying was truncated mid-session by an API quota limit.
citation: Search executed 2026-08-07 across PubMed (E-utilities via connector), OpenAlex and Crossref. Boxing-specific hits were biomechanical, physiological, observational or head-trauma studies; no instructional-method RCT with retention and transfer testing was returned.
verification: search executed 2026-08-07: PubMed queries including 'boxing skill acquisition training intervention', 'boxing training intervention skill randomized controlled trial amateur', 'boxing punch kinematics', 'attentional focus instructions punching velocity impact forces combat athletes'; OpenAlex query sets boxing_skill_acq and boxing_biomech; no qualifying trial returned
ppbf_implication: This is the headline gap for PPBF. Every practice-design recommendation SHADOW makes for boxing currently rests on transfer from other sports or from laboratory tasks. The PPBF pilot should be designed to produce the first boxing-specific retention and transfer data rather than to re-derive general principles.

track: Track 1 - Motor Learning & Skill Acquisition
claim: No evidence base was located that validates individual cue WORDINGS. Evidence attaches to cue CLASSES (external focus, analogy, instruction quantity, autonomy-supportive vs controlling language), not to specific phrases.
study_design: Absence of evidence following structured search
sample_size: 0 studies validating specific cue wordings located
effect_or_estimate: No estimate exists
limitations: Cue wording is plausibly athlete-specific and coach-specific, which may make wording-level validation intrinsically low-yield compared with class-level validation.
citation: Search executed 2026-08-07 across PubMed, OpenAlex and Crossref for coaching cue language and instructional wording; retrieved studies address cue CLASS rather than specific phrasings.
verification: search executed 2026-08-07: PubMed 'coaching cue language instruction athletes attentional' and 'verbal instruction coaching cue athletes wording'; OpenAlex cue_language query set; no wording-level validation study returned
ppbf_implication: The PPBF cue library must state on its face that individual cue text is COACHING CRAFT classified as COACHING/FILM-STUDY INTERPRETATION, and that only the cue CLASS carries evidence. PPBF can then generate its own wording-level effectiveness data through coach review and outcome capture.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Across combat-sport striking studies, straight/reverse punches produce larger mean impact forces than several other upper-limb strikes; the highest mean force reported in the pooled set was 3427 N for a straight punch.
study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis (28 studies, 9 strike types)
effect_or_estimate: Highest reported mean force 3427 N for straight punch; palm strike lower velocity than reverse/straight/junzuki punch
boxing_specific: PARTIAL - pooled across boxing, karate, taekwondo, self-defence
limitations: Pools heterogeneous measurement devices and populations; device differences alone can shift absolute force; not a boxing-only estimate
citation: pooled review: 'Force and velocity of impact during upper limb strikes in combat sports: a systematic review and meta-analysis', Sports Biomechanics
ppbf_implication: SHADOW must NOT treat any absolute punch-force number as a cross-device benchmark. Force fields require a device_id and are only comparable within device.
verified_title: Force and velocity of impact during upper limb strikes in combat sports: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: In Olympic boxers striking an instrumented dummy head, mean punch force was 3427 (SD 811) N, hand velocity 9.14 (SD 2.06) m/s and effective punch mass 2.9 (SD 2.0) kg; force was higher in heavier weight classes primarily via higher effective mass, not higher hand speed.
population: Olympic boxers from five weight classes
study_design: Laboratory biomechanics, Hybrid III instrumented dummy
effect_or_estimate: Force 3427±811 N; velocity 9.14±2.06 m/s; effective mass 2.9±2.0 kg; jaw load 876±288 N; peak translational acceleration 58±13 g
limitations: n=7; straight punches to a dummy face only; laboratory target is not a moving opponent; wide SD on effective mass
citation: Walilko et al., 'Biomechanics of the head for Olympic boxer punches to the face', British Journal of Sports Medicine
ppbf_implication: Supports coaching emphasis on whole-body linkage (effective mass) over pure hand speed. Justifies a curriculum prerequisite that weight transfer and trunk linkage precede power-punch instruction.
verified_title: Biomechanics of the head for Olympic boxer punches to the face.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: During a rear-hand straight punch to a movable head-mass target, reduction in momentum of the punching arm accounted for approximately 95% of the impact impulse, apportioned as roughly 40% upper arm, 35% forearm and 20% fist plus glove.
study_design: Laboratory 3D motion capture plus target-mounted accelerometer
effect_or_estimate: Arm-segment momentum reduction explained ~95% of impulse (40/35/20 split); r=0.902 between peak and impulse of impact force
limitations: n=9; single punch type; describes the ARM segment partition of impulse at impact and does not by itself quantify how much of that arm momentum was generated by the legs and trunk upstream
citation: 'Transfer of momentum from different arm segments to a light movable target during a straight punch thrown by expert boxers', Journal of Sports Sciences
ppbf_implication: Use as the evidence anchor for the 'proximal segments matter' teaching point while explicitly refusing to publish a numeric 'legs contribute X%' figure.
verified_title: Transfer of momentum from different arm segments to a light movable target during a straight punch thrown by expert boxers.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
topic: contested claim: 'power comes from the legs'
claim: The specific quantified coaching claim that a stated percentage of punch power 'comes from the legs' is not supported by a single verifiable boxing biomechanics estimate. Lower-limb kinetics do measurably contribute (dual force-plate GRF and RFD covary with punch output) and lower-body strength/power correlate with punch impact force, but no validated partition of punch force into leg/trunk/arm percentages exists in the boxing literature retrieved.
study_design: Synthesis of force-plate kinetics study, strength-correlation study and review
sample_size: 10 amateur boxers (force plate study); 28 highly trained (strength study)
effect_or_estimate: Cross punch pre-fatigue peak punch force 1475.42 N, GRF 947.54 N, RFD 3973.38 N/s (n=10); lower-body maximal and explosive strength associated with punch impact force in elite amateurs. NO validated percentage partition exists
limitations: Correlational: strength-punch associations are not causal. Absolute forces are device-specific. The colloquial percentage claim is a coaching heuristic, not a measured quantity
citation: 'The Role of Lower Limb Kinetics in Boxing Punches and the Impact of Fatigue on Biomechanical Performance' (Bioengineering) and Beattie & Ruddock, 'The Role of Strength on Punch Impact Force in Boxing' (J Strength Cond Res)
verification: pubmed:PMID 41463652 and PMID 35836314; DOIs returned in records
ppbf_implication: SHADOW cue library must carry 'drive from the floor' as COACHING HEURISTIC with a biomechanical rationale flag, never as a quantified claim. Block any generated text asserting a leg-contribution percentage.
verified_title: The Role of Lower Limb Kinetics in Boxing Punches and the Impact of Fatigue on Biomechanical Performance.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Punch types differ systematically in force and rate of force development, but the rank order is not stable across studies or devices: one force-plate study of senior elite amateurs found the greatest impact force and RFD in the rear hook (2624 +/- 581 N), while a dual-force-plate study of amateur boxers found the cross highest (1475.42 N).
population: Senior elite amateur boxers; amateur boxers
effect_or_estimate: Rear hook 2624±581 N (vertically mounted force plate); cross 1475.42 N (boxing force sensor + dual force plates)
limitations: Different devices, mounting, target compliance and populations. The discrepancy is most parsimoniously explained by measurement method, not by a true reversal of punch mechanics
citation: 'Test-retest reliability and sensitivity of senior elite amateur boxers maximal punch force...' (PLoS ONE) and 'The Role of Lower Limb Kinetics in Boxing Punches...' (Bioengineering)
verification: pubmed:PMID 37561692 and PMID 41463652; DOIs returned in records
ppbf_implication: Rubrics must score punch QUALITY behaviourally, not by force ranking. Any force-based punch comparison in the app must be within-athlete, within-device, within-session.
verified_title: Test-retest reliability and sensitivity of senior elite amateur boxers maximal punch force, as quantified by a vertically mounted force plate.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Lead-hand and rear-hand straight punches differ measurably in kinematics and kinetics in elite boxers, and bilateral asymmetry is a describable, trainable characteristic rather than an error to be eliminated.
study_design: Laboratory 3D motion capture (Vicon) plus two Kistler force plates
effect_or_estimate: Systematic kinematic and kinetic differences between lead (non-dominant) and rear (dominant) straight punches; asymmetry characterised
limitations: Single stance (orthodox) and single handedness; no southpaw comparison; no female sample
citation: 'Kinematic and kinetic differences between lead and rear straight punches in elite boxers: bilateral asymmetry and training implications', BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
ppbf_implication: Rubrics must score lead and rear straights on SEPARATE criteria. SHADOW asymmetry flags must not treat lead/rear force difference as a defect.
verified_title: Kinematic and kinetic differences between lead and rear straight punches in elite boxers: bilateral asymmetry and training implications.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: A boxing dynamometer discriminated maximal rear-hand straight punch force by skill level: elite 4800 +/- 227 N, intermediate 3722 +/- 133 N, novice 2381 +/- 116 N.
effect_or_estimate: Elite 4800±227 N; intermediate 3722±133 N; novice 2381±116 N (rear hand, simulated boxing)
limitations: Small groups; single custom device from 2000; cross-sectional so cannot show that training a novice to a given force produces elite performance; correlation with competitive success not tested
citation: 'Development of a boxing dynamometer and its punch force discrimination efficacy', Journal of Sports Sciences
ppbf_implication: Punch force can serve as a coarse level discriminator on one fixed device, but PPBF must NOT set a force threshold for progression without its own device-specific normative study.
verified_title: Development of a boxing dynamometer and its punch force discrimination efficacy.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Professional-level collegiate boxers showed 22-31% higher punch acceleration and 18-27% greater forefoot plantar pressure than amateur-level peers, with forefoot pressure positively correlated with punch acceleration (r = 0.62-0.71).
study_design: Cross-sectional wearable IMU plus pressure-sensing insoles
effect_or_estimate: Acceleration +22-31%; forefoot pressure +18-27%; r = 0.62-0.71
limitations: Cross-sectional and correlational; cannot establish that training forefoot loading causes higher punch acceleration; n=24; jab and cross only under controlled conditions
citation: 'Wearable Sensor-Based Analysis of Punch Acceleration and Plantar Pressure Distribution in Boxing', Sensors
ppbf_implication: Gives a measurable, observable proxy for the coaching cue 'stay on the balls of the feet / load the front foot' — supports a weight-distribution criterion in the stance rubric, flagged as correlational.
verified_title: Wearable Sensor-Based Analysis of Punch Acceleration and Plantar Pressure Distribution in Boxing.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: A shared phase structure for four boxing punches (lead and rear straight and hook punches) has been defined using synchronised ground reaction force, EMG, high-speed video and striking dynamometry.
effect_or_estimate: Phase definitions established for 4 punch types
limitations: n=10; heavier-than-average sample; phases defined for maximal-effort punches, not in-bout punches
citation: Lenetsky et al., 'Defining the Phases of Boxing Punches: A Mixed-Method Approach', Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
ppbf_implication: Adopt a published phase vocabulary (preparation/execution/impact/retraction) as the SHADOW observation schema for punch rubrics so raters and film-study tags share one language.
verified_title: Defining the Phases of Boxing Punches: A Mixed-Method Approach.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Effective mass is the accepted construct for an athlete's inertial contribution to momentum transfer at strike impact, and a 'double peak muscle activation' pattern has been theorised to enhance hand velocity before impact and joint stiffening during impact.
effect_or_estimate: Concept review; double-peak activation described as theorised, not established
limitations: The double-peak activation mechanism is explicitly presented as theory; effective mass calculation methods vary between authors
citation: 'Is effective mass in combat sports punching above its weight?', Human Movement Science
ppbf_implication: Justifies teaching 'connect then stiffen at impact' as a biomechanically-reasoned cue, tagged as MECHANISM-THEORISED rather than verified.
verified_title: Is effective mass in combat sports punching above its weight?

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Lower-body fatigue reduces punch force. After a 9.5-minute lower-body circuit, punch force declined significantly across all punch types by 4.26% on average, with the largest reductions in the cross and left hook; RFD responses were variable with compensatory increases in some punches.
effect_or_estimate: -4.26% punch force overall (p=0.027); largest decrements in cross and left hook
limitations: n=10; artificial circuit rather than sparring-induced fatigue; single session
citation: 'The Role of Lower Limb Kinetics in Boxing Punches and the Impact of Fatigue on Biomechanical Performance', Bioengineering
ppbf_implication: Every technical rubric needs a fatigued-state observation context. A skill scored only when fresh is not evidence the skill survives round 3.
verified_title: The Role of Lower Limb Kinetics in Boxing Punches and the Impact of Fatigue on Biomechanical Performance.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: An independent study in 28 highly trained amateur boxers found intense intermittent lower-body and trunk exercise (rowing) altered punch force and force-time variables across jab, cross, and lead- and rear-hand hooks.
effect_or_estimate: Significant (p<0.05) differences between non-fatigued and fatigued states across punch types; effect sizes reported
limitations: Rowing is not boxing-specific fatigue; direction and magnitude by punch type not extractable from abstract
citation: 'The effect of fatiguing lower-body exercise on punch forces in highly-trained boxers', European Journal of Sport Science
ppbf_implication: Supports mandatory 'late-round' rubric variants; two independent samples now show fatigue degrades punch output.
verified_title: The effect of fatiguing lower-body exercise on punch forces in highly-trained boxers.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Maximal lower-body strength and explosive strength of both upper and lower body are largely associated with punch impact force in elite amateur boxers; separately, upper- and lower-body strength and power variables relate to punch force-time characteristics in highly trained amateurs.
population: Elite and highly trained amateur boxers
study_design: Narrative review plus cross-sectional correlational study
effect_or_estimate: Associations reported between CMJ / bench throw / isometric measures and punch peak force, impulse and RFD
limitations: Correlational, not causal. Being strong is associated with punching hard; it does not follow that strength training alone raises punch force without technical work
citation: Beattie & Ruddock (J Strength Cond Res) and Dunn et al. (J Strength Cond Res)
verification: pubmed:PMID 35836314 and PMID 32218063; DOIs returned in records
ppbf_implication: Physical-quality track (A-other) owns strength prescription. Track 2 only records that technique rubrics must not be confounded with strength: a stronger athlete can score high on force and low on technique.
verified_title: Relationships Between Punch Impact Force and Upper- and Lower-Body Muscular Strength and Power in Highly Trained Amateur Boxers.
title_consistency_check: MANUALLY REVIEWED — author-year or multi-source citation, record confirmed

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Body height and arm span explained about 36% of the variance in straight punch impact power and 30-34% for other punch categories in 69 boxing practitioners.
effect_or_estimate: BH and AS explained ~36% of straight punch impact power variance; 30-34% for other categories
limitations: Cross-sectional; 'boxing practitioners' is a heterogeneous competitive level; device-specific (PowerKube)
citation: 'Influence of Anthropometric Characteristics and Muscle Performance on Punch Impact', Sports
ppbf_implication: Any SHADOW punch-power metric must be interpreted alongside height/arm span or it will systematically rank taller athletes as more skilled. Flag as a fairness risk in the youth cohort where growth confounds everything.
verified_title: Influence of Anthropometric Characteristics and Muscle Performance on Punch Impact.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: In a randomised-signal backward straight punch task, the boxing group produced the highest impact force at 3.96 +/- 0.45 times body weight, above Tao Lu (Chinese Wushu), Karate and physical-education control groups, with a moderate positive correlation between impact and muscle activation patterns.
population: Boxing, Tao Lu, Karate athletes and PE-student controls
effect_or_estimate: Boxing 3.96±0.45 x body weight, highest of four groups
limitations: Small per-group n (28 total across 4 groups); pendulum target; body-weight normalisation is device- and protocol-specific
citation: 'Analysis of the impact force and key technique of backward straight punch in different combat sports', Scientific Reports
ppbf_implication: Evidence that boxing technique is not interchangeable with other striking styles — supports refusing cross-discipline technical transfer claims in the curriculum without explicit flagging.
verified_title: Analysis of the impact force and key technique of backward straight punch in different combat sports.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Competitive boxers showed measurable long-term baropodometric asymmetry versus non-athlete controls, including greater total foot load on the right foot, greater rearfoot load on the left foot, and an inversion of the rearfoot-to-forefoot load ratio between feet.
effect_or_estimate: TFL right p=0.022; RfL left p=0.011; FfL right vs left p=0.001; ratio inversion p=0.001
limitations: Cross-sectional: cannot distinguish training-induced adaptation from self-selection. No injury or performance outcome measured. Stance side not reported in the abstract
citation: 'Long-term effects of asymmetrical posture in boxing assessed by baropodometry', The Journal of Sports Medicine and Physical Fitness
ppbf_implication: Do NOT build a SHADOW rule that flags boxing stance asymmetry as pathology. Route asymmetry concerns to a qualified clinician; the app records the observation only.
verified_title: Long-term effects of asymmetrical posture in boxing assessed by baropodometry.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Pre-bout standing body sway differed between adult boxers who did and did not report post-bout motion sickness symptoms (dizziness/nausea).
effect_or_estimate: Group difference in pre-bout sway between symptom-reporting and non-reporting boxers
limitations: Association only. Post-bout dizziness/nausea has multiple causes including head impact, dehydration and exertion; this study does not diagnose anything
citation: 'Pre-bout standing body sway differs between adult boxers who do and do not report post-bout motion sickness', PLoS ONE
ppbf_implication: SAFETY BOUNDARY: balance observations are coach-visible signals that trigger a HUMAN medical referral. SHADOW must never interpret sway or dizziness as a concussion determination.
verified_title: Pre-bout standing body sway differs between adult boxers who do and do not report post-bout motion sickness.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Fighters (boxing/muay thai) differed from non-fighter controls in lower-limb muscle responses evoked by electrical vestibular stimulation, indicating altered vestibular balance reflexes.
effect_or_estimate: Significant short and medium latency response differences between fighters and controls
boxing_specific: PARTIAL - boxing and muay thai combined
limitations: Cross-sectional; cannot attribute to head impacts causally; no clinical outcome
citation: 'Altered Vestibular Balance Function in Combat Sport Athletes', Journal of Neurotrauma
ppbf_implication: Balance criteria inside technical rubrics must be scored as SKILL, never repurposed as a neurological screen. Keep the two data streams separated in the schema.
verified_title: Altered Vestibular Balance Function in Combat Sport Athletes.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: A vertically mounted force plate showed excellent within-day and good-to-excellent between-day reliability for peak punch impact force and RFD in senior elite amateur boxers (ICC 0.89-0.99, CV 3-10%), with SEM and smallest worthwhile change permitting detection of small-to-moderate changes.
study_design: Test-retest reliability study over two days
limitations: n=10, all senior elite male; reliability in novices and youth is unknown and likely worse
citation: 'Test-retest reliability and sensitivity of senior elite amateur boxers maximal punch force, as quantified by a vertically mounted force plate', PLoS ONE
ppbf_implication: If PPBF ever acquires force instrumentation, this is the reliability protocol template (two separate days, ICC + CV + SEM + SWC). Reliability MUST be re-established in PPBF's own youth/novice population.
verified_title: Test-retest reliability and sensitivity of senior elite amateur boxers maximal punch force, as quantified by a vertically mounted force plate.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Intrasession and intersession variability and reliability of punching impact kinetics (impulse, peak and mean force) have been quantified separately for untrained participants and experienced boxers across four punch types using CV and ICC.
effect_or_estimate: CV and ICC reported by cohort and punch type (jab, cross, lead and rear hook)
limitations: Abstract does not give the numeric split; reliability differs between cohorts, which is the substantive point
citation: Lenetsky et al., 'Variability and Reliability of Punching Impact Kinetics in Untrained Participants and Experienced Boxers', Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
ppbf_implication: Reliability is population-specific. A rubric or device validated on experienced boxers cannot be assumed reliable on PPBF beginners. This is the single most important measurement caveat for Track 2.
verified_title: Variability and Reliability of Punching Impact Kinetics in Untrained Participants and Experienced Boxers.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Commercially available punch trackers (three consumer devices tested) showed no strong correlations with gold-standard force-plate peak force or with 3D-tracked peak and mean punch velocity during full-contact punches.
population: Male participants performing rear straights, hooks and uppercuts
study_design: Criterion-validity study vs force plate and Qualisys 3D
effect_or_estimate: No strong correlations; MAPE and MPE reported per device variable
limitations: Three specific 2023-era devices; firmware and models change; does not test every product on the market
citation: Omcirk et al., 'Validity of Commercially Available Punch Trackers', Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
ppbf_implication: HARD PRODUCT RULE: SHADOW must not ingest consumer punch-tracker force/velocity as a validated performance measure. If ingested at all, tag source_quality as LOW and exclude from progression decisions. Vendor claims are low-authority.
verified_title: Validity of Commercially Available Punch Trackers.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: A low-cost accelerometer/smartphone system for punch and kick velocity showed only moderate reliability (ICC(3,1) 0.746-0.786; SEM 0.488-0.921 m/s), comparable to commercial systems.
limitations: Low sampling frequency acknowledged by authors; moderate not excellent reliability
citation: 'Reliability of a Low-Cost Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) to Measure Punch and Kick Velocity', Sensors
ppbf_implication: A ~0.5-0.9 m/s SEM is larger than most plausible within-athlete weekly change. Any SHADOW trend line built on such a device would be mostly noise. Set a minimum-detectable-change gate before plotting trends.
verified_title: Reliability of a Low-Cost Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) to Measure Punch and Kick Velocity.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: A commercial impact-power device (PowerKube) produced systematically different readings by strike geometry: level centre strikes 5782 +/- 230 W, level off-centre 4864 +/- 119 W, inclined centre 4500 +/- 220 W (all differences p<0.05), quantified as technical error of measurement.
effect_or_estimate: 5782±230 W vs 4864±119 W vs 4500±220 W by strike geometry
limitations: Laboratory simulated strikes, not human punchers in all conditions
citation: 'Reliability and Practical Use of a Commercial Device for Measuring Punch and Kick Impact Kinetics', Sports
ppbf_implication: Where a punch lands on the target changes the number by >20%. Any PPBF power measurement protocol must fix and record target contact zone, or the metric measures aim rather than power.
verified_title: Reliability and Practical Use of a Commercial Device for Measuring Punch and Kick Impact Kinetics.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: A systematic review of sport-specific performance tests across Olympic combat sports (including amateur boxing) found the majority of studies used samples under 30 participants (74%) and nearly a third lacked sufficient methodological description.
study_design: Systematic review with methodological quality appraisal
effect_or_estimate: 74% of reviewed studies had n<30; ~1/3 with insufficient description
boxing_specific: PARTIAL - includes boxing among six sports
limitations: Review of validation quality rather than of any single test
citation: 'Tests for the Assessment of Sport-Specific Performance in Olympic Combat Sports: A Systematic Review With Practical Recommendations', Frontiers in Physiology
ppbf_implication: Foundational justification for the honest reliability_status='UNVALIDATED - PPBF MUST ESTABLISH' on every rubric row. The field has not solved this; PPBF must not pretend it has.
verified_title: Tests for the Assessment of Sport-Specific Performance in Olympic Combat Sports: A Systematic Review With Practical Recommendations.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
topic: observational rubric inter-rater reliability is achievable but not automatic
claim: Observational movement-rating instruments reach usable inter-rater reliability only with defined criteria and rater training: an FMS-style tool scored by generalist primary-school teachers achieved good inter-rater reliability by ICC for overall movement competence, whereas the Functional Movement Screen scored by 20 qualified physiotherapists acting as untrained raters was studied precisely because untrained-rater agreement is a known problem.
population: School teachers rating children; physiotherapists rating athletes
effect_or_estimate: Good inter-rater reliability (ICC, two-way mixed, absolute agreement) for overall movement competence in the teacher study
limitations: Neither instrument is a boxing instrument. Transfer of the reliability figures to boxing rubrics is NOT justified; only the METHOD transfers
citation: 'Inter-rater reliability of the FMS assessment tool among generalist primary-school teachers' (JSAMS) and Elias, 'The Inter-rater Reliability of the Functional Movement Screen Within an Athletic Population Using Untrained Raters' (JSCR)
verification: pubmed:PMID 40744793 and PMID 23838983; DOIs returned in records
ppbf_implication: PPBF's inter-rater study must report ICC (two-way mixed, absolute agreement) for ordinal totals and weighted kappa for individual criteria, and must test the raters who will actually score: volunteer and assistant coaches, not only the head coach.
verified_title: Inter-rater reliability of the FMS(2) assessment tool among generalist primary-school teachers.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: The Canadian Agility and Movement Skill Assessment demonstrates that a criterion-referenced observational movement assessment can be built with documented feasibility, objectivity and reliability evidence, using expert Delphi face validity followed by field testing in children.
study_design: Instrument development with Delphi expert review and field reliability testing
sample_size: Delphi panel n=19; field sample of children
effect_or_estimate: Feasibility, objectivity and reliability evidence established
limitations: Not boxing; not combat sport; the transferable element is the development pathway, not the content
citation: 'Canadian Agility and Movement Skill Assessment (CAMSA): Validity, objectivity, and reliability evidence for children 8-12 years of age', Journal of Sport and Health Science
ppbf_implication: Adopt this sequence for PPBF rubrics: Delphi with coaches for content validity, then video-based inter-rater study, then live-scoring feasibility, then longitudinal sensitivity to change.
verified_title: Canadian Agility and Movement Skill Assessment (CAMSA): Validity, objectivity, and reliability evidence for children 8-12 years of age.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Inter-rater reliability of an observational alignment scale was successfully established using standardised instructions and lateral video recordings of standardised poses, demonstrating a feasible protocol design for video-based scoring of postural criteria.
effect_or_estimate: Inter-rater reliability of a 3-pose observational scale assessed from lateral video
limitations: Yoga poses are static; boxing skills are dynamic and interactive. Only the video-protocol design transfers
citation: 'Interrater Reliability of an Observational Rating Scale and Video Analysis of Yoga Poses', Journal of Sport Rehabilitation
ppbf_implication: PPBF should run the reliability study on VIDEO first (fixed stimulus, all raters see the same performance), then test live-scoring agreement separately. These are two different reliability questions.
verified_title: Interrater Reliability of an Observational Rating Scale and Video Analysis of Yoga Poses.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Expert and non-expert rater agreement and inter/intra-rater reliability can be established separately for individual skills within an observational movement-pattern assessment system, using filmed performances of children as the fixed stimulus.
effect_or_estimate: Expert-non-expert agreement plus inter- and intra-rater reliability reported per skill
limitations: Fundamental movement skills, not boxing
citation: 'Investigating Expert-Rater Agreement and Inter/Intra-Rater Reliability of Two Fundamental Movement Skills for the Locomotor Subscale...', Perceptual and Motor Skills
ppbf_implication: PPBF must report expert-vs-novice-rater agreement, not just pooled ICC, because assistant coaches and volunteers will do most in-gym scoring.
verified_title: Investigating Expert-Rater Agreement and Inter/Intra-Rater Reliability of Two Fundamental Movement Skills for the Locomotor Subscale of the FG-COMPASS.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Sport-specific classification systems can achieve excellent inter-rater reliability when built on defined test batteries: all three classifier teams agreed on overall class allocation for all athletes in a Para Va'a system, with almost perfect agreement in 14 individual tests.
effect_or_estimate: 100% agreement on class allocation; excellent ICC for trunk, leg and on-water batteries; Fleiss kappa almost perfect in 14 tests
limitations: Different sport and purpose (eligibility classification not skill development); small athlete n
citation: 'Interrater Reliability of the New Sport-Specific Evidence-Based Classification System for Para Va'a', Adapted Physical Activity Quarterly
ppbf_implication: Directly relevant to PPBF's adaptive lane: it is possible to reach near-perfect agreement on banding decisions, but only with explicit test batteries and trained rater teams. Reports Fleiss kappa for multi-rater categorical agreement — the correct statistic when >2 raters assign a band.
verified_title: Interrater Reliability of the New Sport-Specific Evidence-Based Classification System for Para Va'a.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: A systematic review of impairment and activity-limitation measures for evidence-based classification in para sport concluded that measures with the necessary measurement properties are lacking, presenting significant challenges to building an evidence-based system.
effect_or_estimate: Lack of measures with adequate measurement properties identified as the central barrier
limitations: Not boxing; not a technical-skill assessment review
citation: 'Guiding Evidence-Based Classification in Para Sporting Populations: A Systematic Review of Impairment Measures and Activity Limitation Measures', Sports Medicine
ppbf_implication: PPBF's adaptive boxing lane has NO validated technical-skill measurement inheritance available. Every adaptive rubric variant is a PPBF original requiring its own validation. Do not claim otherwise to funders.
verified_title: Guiding Evidence-Based Classification in Para Sporting Populations: A Systematic Review of Impairment Measures and Activity Limitations.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: High contextual interference (random/varied practice order) improves RETENTION in motor learning relative to low interference, confirmed in a meta-analysis of 54 studies using both three-level mixed and random-effects models.
population: Mixed human learners across laboratory and applied tasks
sample_size: 54 studies in meta-analysis (294 full texts screened)
effect_or_estimate: High CI favours retention (both models concordant)
limitations: Dominated by laboratory tasks and novice learners; effects in expert athletes on complex interactive skills are less established; boxing-specific CI trials were not found in this search
citation: 'High contextual interference improves retention in motor learning: systematic review and meta-analysis', Scientific Reports
ppbf_implication: CORE CURRICULUM PRINCIPLE. Blocked practice flatters the session scorecard; random practice produces the learning. SHADOW session logic must schedule blocked practice only in the introduction phase and switch to randomised/varied order for consolidation, and must never treat within-session improvement as evidence of learning.
verified_title: High contextual interference improves retention in motor learning: systematic review and meta-analysis.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Contextual interference produced a medium overall benefit for TRANSFER in motor learning (SMD = 0.55) favouring random practice, across 34 studies in the quantitative synthesis.
population: Laboratory and applied settings, multiple age groups
effect_or_estimate: SMD = 0.55 favouring random practice for transfer
limitations: Same laboratory-dominance caveat; moderators by age and setting were examined but boxing was not a represented sport
citation: 'The effect of contextual interference on transfer in motor learning - a systematic review and meta-analysis', Frontiers in Psychology
ppbf_implication: Justifies the mandatory transfer_test_variant column in the rubric CSV: transfer is the outcome the practice schedule is chosen to produce, so it must be the outcome measured.
verified_title: The effect of contextual interference on transfer in motor learning - a systematic review and meta-analysis.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: The challenge point framework holds that optimal learning occurs when task difficulty is matched to performer skill level, because the information available from performance is maximised at an intermediate level of functional difficulty.
population: Theoretical framework for motor learners generally
study_design: Theoretical framework paper with testable hypotheses
effect_or_estimate: No single effect size; framework generating testable predictions
limitations: A framework, not an empirical result. Its specific predictions require testing in each domain
citation: Guadagnoli & Lee, 'Challenge point: a framework for conceptualizing the effects of various practice conditions in motor learning', Journal of Motor Behavior
ppbf_implication: The theoretical basis for level-banded rubrics and for constraint dosing. SHADOW should propose constraints that raise functional difficulty as competency band rises, with the coach approving the step.
verified_title: Challenge point: a framework for conceptualizing the effects of various practice conditions in motor learning.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Practice with variations of a criterion task produced better retention than practice on the criterion task alone in a force-production task, contradicting a strict specificity-of-learning interpretation.
population: Adult learners in a laboratory force-production task
effect_or_estimate: Variable acquisition practice produced superior retention vs constant practice
limitations: 1990 laboratory force task; considerable distance from interactive boxing skill; specificity vs variability remains a live debate
citation: 'Specificity and variability of practice', Research Quarterly for Exercise and Sport
ppbf_implication: Supports building variability into every drill specification (target height, distance, angle, tempo) rather than fixed-repetition prescription.
verified_title: Specificity and variability of practice.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: An exploratory meta-analytic review of differential learning found it compared favourably with other motor learning methods in acquisition and retention, but the authors themselves note controversy surrounding the theory and describe the review as exploratory.
effect_or_estimate: Favourable pooled effects reported, characterised as exploratory by the authors
limitations: Authors explicitly flag controversy; small heterogeneous literature; risk of small-study and publication bias; no boxing trial identified
citation: 'An Exploratory Meta-Analytic Review on the Empirical Evidence of Differential Learning as an Enhanced Motor Learning Method', Frontiers in Psychology
ppbf_implication: Differential learning may be OFFERED as a coach-selectable practice mode but must be labelled emerging/contested in the SHADOW practice-design engine — not presented as established best practice.
verified_title: An Exploratory Meta-Analytic Review on the Empirical Evidence of Differential Learning as an Enhanced Motor Learning Method.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
topic: differential learning vs contextual interference head-to-head
claim: A controlled comparison of three contextual-interference practice orders and three differential-learning variation schedules in novice basketball players examined effects on both motor learning and motivation, indicating these frameworks are now being tested against each other rather than assumed equivalent.
population: Novice female students learning a basketball jump shot
effect_or_estimate: Seven-arm comparison including a control; outcomes on learning and motivation
limitations: Closed skill (jump shot), female novices, 3 days of practice; short intervention
citation: 'Effect of Contextual Interference and Differential Learning on Motor Skill Development and Motivation in Novice Basketball Players', European Journal of Sport Science
ppbf_implication: A directly copyable design for PPBF's own practice-schedule pilot: several practice orders, a control, and motivation measured alongside skill.
verified_title: Effect of Contextual Interference and Differential Learning on Motor Skill Development and Motivation in Novice Basketball Players.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
topic: external focus of attention - the meta-analytic claim
claim: Meta-analysis of 73 studies (1,824 participants) reported an external focus of attention superior to an internal focus for motor performance, with a small pooled effect (Hedges' g = 0.264, 95% CI 0.217-0.310), and separate analyses for retention and transfer learning.
effect_or_estimate: Hedges' g = 0.264 (95% CI 0.217-0.310) for performance
limitations: Small effect; superseded in part by the reanalysis in claim A2-038
citation: 'Superiority of external attentional focus for motor performance and learning: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses', Psychological Bulletin
ppbf_implication: Read together with A2-038 before any cue-library rule is written.
verified_title: Superiority of external attentional focus for motor performance and learning: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
topic: external focus - CONTESTED by publication-bias reanalysis
claim: A robust Bayesian reanalysis of the external-focus literature, incorporating several plausible models of publication bias, found moderate to strong evidence of publication bias and concluded that the apparent external-focus superiority is substantially attributable to reporting bias.
population: Same underlying literature as the prior meta-analyses
study_design: Robust Bayesian meta-analysis and systematic review of seven prior meta-studies
effect_or_estimate: Moderate-to-strong evidence of publication bias; external-focus advantage not robust to bias-adjusted models
limitations: A reanalysis, not new primary data; bias-adjusted models involve modelling assumptions of their own
citation: 'Reporting bias, not external focus: A robust Bayesian meta-analysis and systematic review of the external focus of attention literature', Psychological Bulletin
ppbf_implication: MUST-RECONCILE FOR SYNTHESIS. SHADOW's cue library cannot state 'external cues are better' as settled fact. Present both cue types, record which was used and the athlete response, and let PPBF's own data accumulate. This is a genuine live scientific dispute in 2026.
verified_title: Reporting bias, not external focus: A robust Bayesian meta-analysis and systematic review of the external focus of attention literature.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: A network meta-analysis of attentional foci (external, internal, holistic, switching) on the acquisition of SPORT-SPECIFIC motor tasks in healthy adults was conducted following PRISMA and Cochrane methods, extending the focus question beyond laboratory tasks.
study_design: Systematic review with network meta-analysis of RCTs
effect_or_estimate: Network comparison of four focus types
limitations: Healthy adults; heterogeneous sports; does not include boxing-specific trials in the abstract
citation: 'The effectiveness of different attentional foci on the acquisition of sport-specific motor skills in healthy adults: a systematic review with network meta-analysis', PeerJ
ppbf_implication: Supports offering holistic and switching cue options in the SHADOW cue library rather than a binary external/internal toggle.
verified_title: The effectiveness of different attentional foci on the acquisition of sport-specific motor skills in healthy adults: a systematic review with network meta-analysis.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Reduced relative frequency of augmented feedback benefits learning relative to constant feedback in classic experiments supporting the guidance hypothesis: high-frequency physical guidance produced the poorest retention and both high-frequency feedback conditions produced the least learning.
study_design: Controlled experiment crossing feedback type and relative frequency
effect_or_estimate: High-frequency physical guidance produced poorest retention
limitations: 1994 laboratory movement task; later work (see A2-041) shows the guidance effect is not universal, so this is a principle with boundary conditions rather than a law
citation: 'Effects of physical guidance and knowledge of results on motor learning: support for the guidance hypothesis', Research Quarterly for Exercise and Sport
ppbf_implication: Coach-facing guidance: constant correction during pad work inflates in-drill performance and may suppress learning. SHADOW should prompt coaches to fade feedback across a skill's introduction-to-consolidation arc.
verified_title: Effects of physical guidance and knowledge of results on motor learning: support for the guidance hypothesis.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: The reduced-feedback principle has documented exceptions: augmented kinematic feedback in rifle shooting produced group differences only at delayed no-feedback retention tests rather than during acquisition, and separate work reports conditions under which continuous feedback benefits learning of a novel coordination pattern.
population: Rifle shooters; adults learning novel coordination patterns
study_design: RCT with 2- and 10-day retention tests (n=40, 480 shots); plus separate experimental work on continuous auditory feedback
effect_or_estimate: No between-group differences during acquisition; differences emerged at retention
limitations: Different tasks; the exceptions do not overturn the guidance hypothesis but bound it
citation: 'The effects of augmented kinematic feedback on motor skill learning in rifle shooting' (J Sports Sci) and 'More Feedback Is Better than Less: Learning a Novel Upper Limb Joint Coordination Pattern with Augmented Auditory Feedback' (Front Neurosci)
ppbf_implication: Reinforces the central Track 2 message: acquisition-phase performance is a poor predictor of learning. The rifle study is the cleanest demonstration that groups can look identical during practice and differ at retention.
verified_title: The effects of augmented kinematic feedback on motor skill learning in rifle shooting.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Meta-analysis of 29 studies (1,147 participants) found self-controlled feedback gave no significant advantage during acquisition but facilitated motor skill learning in both retention and transfer phases compared with passively received and yoked feedback.
effect_or_estimate: Null in acquisition; positive in retention and transfer
limitations: Effects on autonomy-support are debated: a separate meta-analysis reported reduced feedback frequency and autonomy support had trivial effects on a golf putting task, and a preregistered study found choice failed to enhance retention
citation: 'Self-Controlled Feedback and Behavioral Outcomes in Motor Skill Learning: A Meta-Analysis', Behavioral Sciences
ppbf_implication: Athlete-requested feedback ('ask for the replay') is a low-cost, evidence-supported feature. Note it is exactly the pattern where acquisition and learning diverge — build it and measure it at retention.
verified_title: Self-Controlled Feedback and Behavioral Outcomes in Motor Skill Learning: A Meta-Analysis.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Autonomy-support effects are not robust: a study of a golf putting task found autonomy support and reduced feedback frequency had trivial effects on learning and performance, and a preregistered manipulation found increased perceptions of autonomy through choice failed to enhance motor skill retention.
population: Adult learners, golf putting and cup-stacking
study_design: Controlled experiments including one preregistered study
effect_or_estimate: Trivial effects; failure to replicate retention benefit of choice
limitations: Task-specific; does not negate the meta-analytic retention finding but bounds it
citation: 'Autonomy support and reduced feedback frequency have trivial effects on learning and performance of a golf putting task' (Human Movement Science) and 'Increased perceptions of autonomy through choice fail to enhance motor skill retention' (J Exp Psychol Hum Percept Perform)
ppbf_implication: Do not over-engineer autonomy features on the assumption they are proven. Log usage and outcome; treat as a hypothesis PPBF can test.
verified_title: Autonomy support and reduced feedback frequency have trivial effects on learning and performance of a golf putting task.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Self-controlled video feedback facilitated the learning of TACTICAL skills in tennis in intermediately skilled players, and self-control over combined video feedback and expert modelling facilitated motor learning of a golf chip shot with retention and transfer tests administered.
population: Intermediate tennis players; adult golf learners
study_design: Two controlled studies with yoked control groups
sample_size: 23 tennis players; golf study n not in abstract
effect_or_estimate: Self-controlled group outperformed yoked group on tactical performance measured by a custom tool
limitations: Tennis and golf, not boxing; small samples; coach-delivered attentional cueing was bundled with the video in the tennis study
citation: 'Self-Controlled Video Feedback Facilitates the Learning of Tactical Skills in Tennis' (RQES) and 'Self-control over combined video feedback and modeling facilitates motor learning' (Human Movement Science)
ppbf_implication: Supports SHADOW's film-study lane for TACTICAL learning specifically, with athlete-initiated replay. Note the tennis effect was on tactical, not technical, performance.
verified_title: Self-Controlled Video Feedback Facilitates the Learning of Tactical Skills in Tennis.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
topic: video feedback in a classic sport trial
claim: In an early controlled trial, video-feedback training of the tennis service was compared against traditional training and a no-training control over five weeks in players with at least two years' experience, establishing the design template for sport video-feedback trials.
effect_or_estimate: Three-arm comparison over 5 weeks, twice weekly, 40 min sessions
limitations: 1989 study; effect direction not extractable from the abstract text retrieved
citation: 'The effect of video-feedback on the learning of the tennis service by intermediate players', Journal of Sports Sciences
ppbf_implication: Design template only: three arms, matched contact time, a genuine no-intervention control.
verified_title: The effect of video-feedback on the learning of the tennis service by intermediate players.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: A six-week tennis serving intervention manipulating task representativeness (serve only vs serve-return vs serve+3) directly tested whether higher representativeness improves transfer of serving skill, using a validated representative practice assessment tool to classify task representativeness.
study_design: Six-week three-group intervention with pre/post skill testing
effect_or_estimate: 56 serves twice weekly for 6 weeks across three representativeness levels
limitations: Tennis serve is self-paced; boxing skills are opposed and reactive, arguably making representativeness MORE important, but that is inference
citation: 'Enhancing skill transfer in tennis using representative learning design', Journal of Sports Sciences
ppbf_implication: The core justification for the PPBF constrained-sparring ladder: skills practised without an opponent's information are being practised in a non-representative environment and may not transfer.
verified_title: Enhancing skill transfer in tennis using representative learning design.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: A consensus-based tool for coaches to rapidly assess the representativeness of practice tasks was developed via a four-round Delphi process with 10 academic and 13 coaching experts, reaching consensus on seven items each with two sub-questions.
effect_or_estimate: Seven-item consensus tool
limitations: Tennis-specific item wording; requires re-specification for boxing
citation: 'Helping coaches apply the principles of representative learning design: validation of a tennis specific practice assessment tool', Journal of Sports Sciences
ppbf_implication: DIRECTLY ACTIONABLE: PPBF should build a boxing Representative Practice Assessment Tool by the same Delphi method, so SHADOW can score every drill for representativeness and surface 'this route is all non-representative practice' to the coach.
verified_title: Helping coaches apply the principles of representative learning design: validation of a tennis specific practice assessment tool.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Match simulation practice may not represent competitive match play: analysis in professional Australian football found constraint interactions and their frequencies in training tasks differed from competition, and a separate study concluded match simulations did not reproduce competitive demands.
study_design: Observational comparison of training vs competition constraint profiles
effect_or_estimate: Differences in pressure and time-in-possession constraint interactions between competition, match simulations and small-sided games
limitations: Team invasion sport; boxing has a different constraint structure
citation: 'Applications of a working framework for the measurement of representative learning design in Australian football' (PLoS ONE) and 'Match simulation practice may not represent competitive match play in professional Australian football' (J Sports Sci)
ppbf_implication: Even coaches who believe they are simulating competition frequently are not. SHADOW should compare the constraint profile of assigned drills against the recorded profile of sparring/competition and flag the gap.
verified_title: Applications of a working framework for the measurement of representative learning design in Australian football.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Reviews of perceptual-cognitive skill training conclude that retention and transfer to the field is the outcome that matters and remains the key unresolved design problem, and a classification framework has been proposed to predict which modified perceptual training tasks will transfer.
effect_or_estimate: No pooled effect; both papers frame transfer as the open question
limitations: Opinion/framework pieces rather than meta-analyses
citation: 'Perceptual-cognitive skill training and its transfer to expert performance in the field: future research directions' (Eur J Sport Sci) and 'Modified perceptual training in sport: A new classification framework' (JSAMS)
ppbf_implication: Treat any generic 'sports vision' or reaction-light product as unproven for boxing transfer. Vendor claims are low-authority under the source-priority rule.
verified_title: Perceptual-cognitive skill training and its transfer to expert performance in the field: future research directions.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
topic: perceptual training with coupled motor practice
claim: Video/point-light temporal-occlusion anticipation training COMBINED with motor practice of the observed movement pattern improved anticipation in emerging expert cricket batsmen relative to a control group, with transfer tests to different bowlers.
population: Emerging expert cricket batsmen from a state squad
study_design: Randomised controlled intervention with transfer tests
effect_or_estimate: Intervention group improved anticipation to significantly above chance; control did not
limitations: n=12; striking sport but ball-based; the coupling of perception with action is the transferable design principle
citation: 'Visual-perceptual training with motor practice of the observed movement pattern improves anticipation in emerging expert cricket batsmen', Journal of Sports Sciences
ppbf_implication: If PPBF builds anticipation training, it must keep perception coupled to a movement response (slip, step, parry) rather than a button press or a screen tap.
verified_title: Visual-perceptual training with motor practice of the observed movement pattern improves anticipation in emerging expert cricket batsmen.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
topic: implicit perceptual-motor decision training in combat sport
claim: A 12-session implicit perceptual-motor training programme improved decision-making accuracy in highly skilled junior female karate fighters on a video-based test, where a matched motor-training placebo group did not.
population: Highly skilled junior female karate fighters (mean age 15.7 y)
study_design: Controlled intervention with placebo group and gaze tracking
effect_or_estimate: Only the implicit perceptual-motor group improved video-based decision accuracy
boxing_specific: PARTIAL - karate, a striking combat sport
limitations: Very small groups (n=6); improvement demonstrated on a video-based test with on-mat testing also conducted; single squad
citation: 'Effect of Implicit Perceptual-Motor Training on Decision-Making Skills and Underpinning Gaze Behavior in Combat Athletes', Perceptual and Motor Skills
ppbf_implication: Closest available evidence that decision training works in a striking combat sport, and it is thin (n=18, karate, female juniors). Any PPBF decision-training claim must carry that caveat explicitly.
verified_title: Effect of Implicit Perceptual-Motor Training on Decision-Making Skills and Underpinning Gaze Behavior in Combat Athletes.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Expert karate fighters were more accurate and faster than less-skilled counterparts at blocking and counterattacking, and picked up a repeating attack pattern after the fifth repetition where novices did not.
study_design: In situ decision-making experiment with manipulated attack probability
effect_or_estimate: Experts detected the repeating pattern by the fifth repetition; novices did not
limitations: Karate rules and distances differ from boxing; cross-sectional expert-novice design cannot show trainability
citation: 'Do karate fighters use situational probability information to improve decision-making performance during on-mat tasks?', Journal of Sports Sciences
ppbf_implication: Grounds the 'pattern reading' competency in the tactical curriculum as an observable, testable behaviour: does the athlete adjust after a repeated opponent action?
verified_title: Do karate fighters use situational probability information to improve decision-making performance during on-mat tasks?

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Expertise facilitated transfer of anticipation skill across domains: expert karate athletes anticipated and responded to stimulus skills derived from taekwondo and Australian football in ecologically valid in situ temporal-occlusion tasks better than less expert groups.
population: Expert karate, near-expert karate and novices
sample_size: three groups, n not in abstract
effect_or_estimate: Experts transferred anticipation skill to unfamiliar domains
limitations: Cross-sectional; supports general-principle transfer in experts, which does not imply novices transfer
citation: 'Expertise facilitates the transfer of anticipation skill across domains', Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology
ppbf_implication: Transfer is an expertise-dependent phenomenon. PPBF should not assume a novice's cross-sport athleticism transfers to boxing reading; test it.
verified_title: Expertise facilitates the transfer of anticipation skill across domains.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: In a boxing-specific Simon-like task, expert boxers' incidental responses resembled counterattacks, beginner boxers' resembled defensive responses, and non-athletes showed no punch-direction influence — indicating experience shapes automatic response tendencies to punch stimuli.
sample_size: three groups, n not in abstract
effect_or_estimate: Distinct response patterns by expertise level despite no instruction to attend to punch direction
limitations: Laboratory key-press task, not ring behaviour; cross-sectional
citation: 'What boxing-related stimuli reveal about response behaviour', Journal of Sports Sciences
ppbf_implication: Rare boxing-specific perceptual evidence, and it maps to a curriculum ordering hypothesis: defensive response tendencies appear before counter tendencies. Testable in PPBF's own cohort.
verified_title: What boxing-related stimuli reveal about response behaviour.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: In a boxing-specific spatial attention task mimicking feint-punch combinations, boxers and non-boxers showed significantly longer reaction times to a punch thrown on the same side as a preceding cue, consistent with inhibition-of-return effects operating on feint-punch timing.
effect_or_estimate: Longer RT to same-side punch following a cue
limitations: Screen-based task; cue-target intervals fixed by the experiment, not by a live opponent
citation: 'Timing a fake punch: Inhibitory effects in a boxing-specific spatial attention task', Human Movement Science
ppbf_implication: Gives feint instruction a mechanistic rationale (attentional cueing and its time course) rather than pure tradition, while stopping well short of prescribing feint timings in seconds.
verified_title: Timing a fake punch: Inhibitory effects in a boxing-specific spatial attention task.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: A review of deceptive actions across interactive sports concluded that expertise is central to recognising deception and summarised the cognitive mechanisms proposed to underlie processing of deceptive actions.
population: Athletes across interactive sports including martial arts
effect_or_estimate: Expertise-dependent recognition of deception across disciplines
boxing_specific: PARTIAL - martial arts among several sports
limitations: Review scattered across disciplines and decades; no pooled effect
citation: 'How to Trick Your Opponent: A Review Article on Deceptive Actions in Interactive Sports', Frontiers in Psychology
ppbf_implication: Supports placing feint/deception LATE in the curriculum: the counter-skill (reading deception) is expertise-dependent, so feints against novices teach the feinter bad habits.
verified_title: How to Trick Your Opponent: A Review Article on Deceptive Actions in Interactive Sports.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Elite male amateur boxing (3x3 min) requires maintaining approximately 1.4 actions per second, comprising about 20 punches, 2.5 defensive movements and 47 vertical hip movements per minute across three rounds of about 200 s.
population: Elite male amateur boxers in Olympic semifinal and final bouts
effect_or_estimate: ~1.4 actions/s; ~20 punches, ~2.5 defensive movements, ~47 vertical hip movements per minute
limitations: Pre-2013-rules Olympic footage; elite ceiling values, not youth or novice targets
citation: 'The activity profile of elite male amateur boxing', International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance
ppbf_implication: Defines the observable action vocabulary SHADOW should count (punches, defensive movements, vertical hip movements). These are ELITE reference values, never youth targets.
verified_title: The activity profile of elite male amateur boxing.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: In elite male amateur bouts, winners had higher total punches landed and a lower thrown-to-landed ratio than losers in round 3, higher rear-hand hook landed in rounds 2 and 3, and used fewer defensive movements; the authors note technical discrimination between winners and losers is limited.
effect_or_estimate: Punches landed p=0.041; thrown:landed ratio p=0.027; rear-hand hook landed p=0.038 (R2) and p=0.016 (R3); defensive movements p=0.036
limitations: Judging is subjective, so 'winning' is partly a judging artefact (see A2-063). Authors explicitly caution the discrimination is limited. Association, not causation: throwing more accurate punches may reflect winning rather than cause it
citation: 'The activity profile of elite male amateur boxing', IJSPP
ppbf_implication: Accuracy (landed/thrown) is the most defensible single performance ratio SHADOW can track. Do not build a 'win probability' model on these coefficients.
verified_title: The activity profile of elite male amateur boxing.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: In novice-level amateur bouts (3x2 min), winners landed 18 +/- 11 more punches than losers, applying more lead-hand punches in round 1 (34.2 +/- 10.9 vs 26.5 +/- 9.4), more total punches to the head (121.3 +/- 10.2 vs 96.0 +/- 9.8), more block-and-counterpunch combinations across all rounds (2.8 +/- 1.1 vs 0.1 +/- 0.2) and more punching combinations in rounds 1 and 3 (44.3 +/- 6.4 vs 28.8 +/- 6.7).
study_design: Notational analysis with post-bout blood lactate
effect_or_estimate: Block-and-counter combinations 2.8±1.1 vs 0.1±0.2 (all p<0.05); peak post-bout [La] 11.8±1.6 mmol/L in 16 boxers
limitations: Observational and correlational; small n; single competition context; 3x2 min format
citation: 'Amateur boxing: activity profile of winners and losers', International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance
ppbf_implication: MOST IMPORTANT CURRICULUM FINDING FOR NOVICES. Lead-hand volume and the block-counter unit distinguish novice winners; the 2.8 vs 0.1 gap for block-and-counter is the largest behavioural separation in the retrieved literature. Prioritise lead hand and block-counter in the novice route — flagged as association, not proof of causation.
verified_title: Amateur boxing: activity profile of winners and losers.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Notational analysis of 26 elite male competitors under the Ten Point Must System found winners punched more accurately, with behavioural measures including guard-drop time, movement style, clinch time and interaction time recorded alongside technical measures.
population: Elite male competitors at a national championship
study_design: Notational analysis with self-reported effort and fatigue
effect_or_estimate: Winners punched more accurately; behavioural and technical measures compared
limitations: Subjective judging system defines the outcome; self-report used for effort and fatigue
citation: 'Human behaviours associated with dominance in elite amateur boxing bouts: A comparison of winners and losers under the Ten Point Must-System', PLoS ONE
ppbf_implication: GUARD-DROP TIME is a directly observable, countable variable with a competition-behaviour basis. Adopt it as a rubric criterion for the guard skill instead of the aesthetic 'keeps hands up'.
verified_title: Human behaviours associated with dominance in elite amateur boxing bouts: A comparison of winners and losers under the Ten Point Must System.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Elite female amateur boxing (4x2 min at the time of study) showed an activity rate of about 1.6 actions/s including about 16 punches, 3.3 defensive movements and 63 vertical hip movements per minute; winners maintained higher activity in rounds 1-2, higher movement rate in rounds 2-4 and greater punch accuracy in round 3.
effect_or_estimate: ~1.6 actions/s; ~16 punches/min; ~3.3 defensive movements/min; ~63 vertical hip movements/min
limitations: Superseded round format (4x2 min); 18 bouts; profiles differ from male values so male norms must not be applied to female athletes
citation: 'Performance Analysis of Elite Female Amateur Boxers and Comparison With Their Male Counterparts', IJSPP
ppbf_implication: SHADOW must hold sex-specific reference profiles and must never display a male norm to a female athlete. Note the round format has since changed to 3x3 min.
verified_title: Performance Analysis of Elite Female Amateur Boxers and Comparison With Their Male Counterparts.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
topic: female elite notational analysis under current format
claim: Notational analysis of the 12 final bouts of the 2023 IBA Women's World Boxing Championships under the current 3x3-min format recorded 1,323 offensive and 1,456 defensive actions and computed Offensive and Defensive Effectiveness Ratios to distinguish winners from losers.
population: Elite female boxers at world championship finals
study_design: Notational analysis with a defined offensive-defensive interaction cycle framework
effect_or_estimate: OER and DER computed per boxer
limitations: Finals only (a selected, high-quality subsample); 12 bouts; single championship
citation: 'Notational Analysis of the Final Matches of the 2023 IBA Women's World Boxing Championships', Journal of Functional Morphology and Kinesiology
ppbf_implication: Offensive/Defensive Effectiveness Ratio is a published, reproducible metric definition SHADOW can adopt directly for its film-study schema, with the citation attached.
verified_title: Notational Analysis of the Final Matches of the 2023 IBA Women's World Boxing Championships.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Boxing outcomes are partly a product of subjective officiating: bouts ending in points decisions had a significantly higher proportion of home wins than those decided by knockout in European championship boxing, and an experimental study found a scoring discrepancy attributable to referees' visual access to one ring zone.
population: European championship boxing; certified international referees
study_design: Archival analysis of bout outcomes; counterbalanced experimental officiating study
effect_or_estimate: Higher home-win proportion for points decisions vs knockouts; significant Zone D scoring discrepancy under traditional ropes (F(5,90)=2.442, p=.040)
limitations: Home advantage has multiple causes; the officiating study is small and single-context
citation: 'Do judges enhance home advantage in European championship boxing?' (J Sports Sci) and 'Ergonomic Solutions for Referee Mistakes: A Visual Assessment of the Environment in Boxing Competitions' (Percept Mot Skills)
ppbf_implication: CRITICAL FOR THE DATA MODEL: bout result is a NOISY, partly biased label. SHADOW must never train a skill model on win/loss as ground truth. Use coded technical behaviour as the outcome, with result recorded separately as context.
verified_title: Do judges enhance home advantage in European championship boxing?

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: The 2013 amateur rules change measurably altered boxing technique: post-2013 elite bouts showed fewer total punches thrown, fewer rear-hand punches and rear-hand hooks, fewer punches landed, fewer uppercuts and fewer body punches, with more ring movement and more defensive movements.
study_design: Comparative notational analysis pre- vs post-rule change
effect_or_estimate: All listed technique reductions p<0.05; movement and defensive movement increases p<0.004
limitations: Observational comparison across different competitions and eras; headguard removal and scoring changes are confounded
citation: 'Comparison of amateur boxing before and after the 2013 rules change and the impact on boxers' safety', British Journal of Sports Medicine
ppbf_implication: GOVERNANCE-CRITICAL: technical norms are rule-dependent and therefore have expiry dates. Every SHADOW technical reference value must carry the ruleset and year it was derived under, and be re-validated when rules change.
verified_title: Comparison of amateur boxing before and after the 2013 rules change and the impact on boxers' safety.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Reaction time of the rear straight lengthened during sparring load in the precompetition period after the third round (to 390 ms) compared with the competition period (310 ms), and lead-straight reaction time lengthened between rounds 1 and 3 during precompetition with no such change during the competition period.
study_design: Repeated-measures sparring study across two training periods
effect_or_estimate: Rear straight RT 390 ms (precompetition R3) vs 310 ms (competition period); lead straight lengthened R1 to R3 in precompetition (p<=0.05)
limitations: n=7; training-period comparison is confounded with training state, taper and motivation
citation: 'Effects of Sparring Load on Reaction Speed and Punch Force During the Precompetition and Competition Periods in Boxing', Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
ppbf_implication: Supports round-3 skill degradation as a real, measurable phenomenon and justifies the fatigued-state rubric variant. n=7 means these millisecond values are illustrative, not normative.
verified_title: Effects of Sparring Load on Reaction Speed and Punch Force During the Precompetition and Competition Periods in Boxing.

track: A2-technical-curriculum
claim: Sports visual abilities measured on a commercial sensory station correlated with in-competition punching accuracy in 26 highly trained male amateur boxers, with a parallel study conducted in female amateur boxers.
sex: male study and separate female study
effect_or_estimate: Correlations between visual ability measures and competition punch accuracy
limitations: Cross-sectional and correlational; commercial test battery; does not show visual training improves boxing
citation: 'Relationship between visual ability assessment and punch performance in competition in male amateur boxers' (Front Physiol) and 'The relationship between visual ability assessment and competitive boxing performance in female amateur boxers' (Front Physiol)
