topic: Concussion education for coaches and parents
claim: A systematic review examined the effectiveness of concussion education programmes for coaches and parents of youth athletes.
population: coaches and parents of youth athletes
effect_or_estimate: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE - findings not extracted from the retrieved record
limitations: Existence and topic verified; conclusions not extracted.
citation: A Systematic Review of the Effectiveness of Concussion Education Programs for Coaches and Parents of Youth Athletes. Int J Environ Res Public Health 2020.
verification: pubmed:PMID 32294972 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.3390/ijerph17082665
ppbf_implication: Read before building PPBF's own coach and guardian concussion education module - do not build from scratch.
verified_title: A Systematic Review of the Effectiveness of Concussion Education Programs for Coaches and Parents of Youth Athletes.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: A systematic review and meta-analysis of participation patterns found that predictors of junior versus senior elite performance are opposite: compared with national-class counterparts, adult world-class athletes had MORE childhood/adolescent multi-sport coach-led practice, a LATER main-sport start, LESS main-sport practice and SLOWER initial progress, whereas higher-performing juniors had an earlier main-sport start, more main-sport practice, less other-sports practice and faster initial progress; peer-led play had negligible effects.
population: athletes from local to Olympic level across diverse sports
competitive_level: junior and adult, national-class to world-class
sample_size: 71 study reports, 262 athlete samples, 685 effect sizes, 9,241 athletes
effect_or_estimate: Cohen's d between |0.23| and |0.50| for adult world-class predictors, |0.23| to |0.61| for junior predictors, all p<0.001; GRADE moderate to high except peer-led play (low)
transfer_status: OTHER SPORTS - diverse sports, results reported robust across sport types; boxing not separately analysed
limitations: Retrospective participation data are subject to recall bias. Results robust across sport types but boxing is not identified as a separate stratum.
citation: Predictors of Junior Versus Senior Elite Performance are Opposite: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Participation Patterns. Sports Med 2022.
verification: pubmed:PMID 35038142 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1007/s40279-021-01625-4
ppbf_implication: THE key youth-policy finding. A programme optimised to produce good 15-year-old boxers is, on this evidence, not the programme that produces good 25-year-old boxers. PPBF should encourage multi-sport participation and resist early main-sport concentration.
verified_title: Predictors of Junior Versus Senior Elite Performance are Opposite: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Participation Patterns.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: A critical review of the Long-Term Athlete Development model found a number of problems not necessarily transparent to coaches: the model is one-dimensional and primarily physiological, there is a lack of empirical evidence on which it is based, interpretations are restricted because the underlying data rely on questionable assumptions and erroneous methodologies, and it is a generic model rather than an individualised plan; the authors argue it should be seen as a work in progress.
population: youth athletes in systems that adopted LTAD
effect_or_estimate: Categorical critique; the 'windows of opportunity' construct specifically identified as under-evidenced
transfer_status: general youth sport - directly applicable because LTAD is adopted by boxing federations
limitations: A critique, not an empirical test. LTAD's general principles (individualise, account for maturation) remain defensible.
citation: The long-term athlete development model: physiological evidence and application. J Sports Sci 2011.
verification: pubmed:PMID 21259156 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1080/02640414.2010.536849
ppbf_implication: PPBF must NOT build progression gates that assume a closing developmental window. Say openly in any LTAD-referencing material that the evidence base is contested.
verified_title: The long-term athlete development model: physiological evidence and application.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: A review of long-term athletic development models argued that while maximising sporting talent is one goal, ensuring youth of all ages and abilities receive a strategic plan for health and physical fitness is also important, and provided a comparative examination of the most prominent models.
effect_or_estimate: Conceptual - a pathway for all youth, not only the talented
limitations: Conceptual review; not an empirical comparison of model outcomes.
citation: Long-term athletic development- part 1: a pathway for all youth. J Strength Cond Res 2015.
verification: pubmed:PMID 25486295 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1519/JSC.0000000000000756
ppbf_implication: Aligns with PPBF's nonprofit mission: the development pathway must serve participation and health outcomes, not only competitive selection.
verified_title: Long-term athletic development- part 1: a pathway for all youth.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: The companion review identified that existing structures within competitive youth sport, together with widespread physical inactivity in modern youth, act as barriers to the success of any long-term athletic development pathway, and proposed solutions.
effect_or_estimate: Conceptual
limitations: Commentary rather than empirical study.
citation: Long-term athletic development, part 2: barriers to success and potential solutions. J Strength Cond Res 2015.
verification: pubmed:PMID 25909962 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1519/01.JSC.0000465424.75389.56
ppbf_implication: Supports PPBF designing around the barriers it actually faces (transport, attendance, deconditioning) - already partly modelled in pilot.transportation/attendance barrier tracking (Module 096).
verified_title: Long-term athletic development, part 2: barriers to success and potential solutions.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: A mixed-methods survey of 236 practitioners found that they recognised responsibility for delivering long-term athletic development, were familiar with existing models and reported high adherence focused on health and wellbeing, but that practices associated with growth and maturity, monitoring and assessment, and systematic progression and individualisation were weaker.
population: practitioners delivering youth athletic development (sport coaches, PE teachers)
effect_or_estimate: Self-reported adherence high on health/wellbeing; weaker on maturation, monitoring and individualisation
limitations: Self-report; no observation of actual practice; sampling not representative of boxing coaches specifically.
citation: Optimising long-term athletic development: An investigation of practitioners' knowledge, adherence, practices and challenges. PLoS One 2022.
verification: pubmed:PMID 35077515 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0262995
ppbf_implication: The gap this study names - maturation, monitoring, individualisation - is precisely what a well-designed SHADOW could support. That is a defensible product rationale.
verified_title: Optimising long-term athletic development: An investigation of practitioners' knowledge, adherence, practices and challenges.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
topic: Youth specialisation guidelines - lack of consensus
claim: A systematic review of 23 sport-organisation guidelines across soccer, basketball, ice hockey and swimming found consensus on only 2 of 15 framework items - emphasis on early skill development and access to well-trained coaches - with volume recommendations inconsistent between and within sports and no group proposing methods to monitor athlete wellbeing.
effect_or_estimate: Consensus on 2 of 15 framework items; volume recommendations inconsistent
boxing_specific: no - soccer, basketball, ice hockey, swimming
limitations: Guidelines published 2000-2018; boxing not among the sports reviewed.
citation: Current Sport Organization Guidelines From the AMSSM 2019 Youth Early Sport Specialization Research Summit. Sports Health 2021.
verification: pubmed:PMID 34668454 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1177/19417381211051383
ppbf_implication: There is NO agreed youth training-volume number in sport governance. Anyone quoting one to PPBF must produce its source. PPBF should not invent one either.
verified_title: Current Sport Organization Guidelines From the AMSSM 2019 Youth Early Sport Specialization Research Summit.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: A systematic review of health organisation guidelines and position statements on youth sport specialisation (11 of 56 articles meeting criteria) synthesised recommendations across a 15-item framework covering psychological development, physical development and load, facilities and resources, and timing and monitoring of specialisation.
effect_or_estimate: Framework synthesis; detailed consensus levels not extracted
limitations: Guideline synthesis rather than primary evidence.
citation: Systematic Review of Health Organization Guidelines Following the AMSSM 2019 Youth Early Sport Specialization Summit. Sports Health 2021.
verification: pubmed:PMID 34668459 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1177/19417381211051371
ppbf_implication: Use the 15-item framework as the checklist against which PPBF's own youth policy is written and audited.
verified_title: Systematic Review of Health Organization Guidelines Following the AMSSM 2019 Youth Early Sport Specialization Summit.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: A multidisciplinary scoping systematic review of youth sport specialisation (40 empirical publications from 906 screened) concluded that a thorough understanding of the phenomenon is still lacking and that the lack of synthesis makes existing practical recommendations potentially tenuous.
effect_or_estimate: Categorical: recommendations described as potentially tenuous
limitations: Scoping review; heterogeneous definitions of specialisation across the literature.
citation: Youth sport specialization: a multidisciplinary scoping systematic review. J Sports Sci 2019.
verification: pubmed:PMID 31135271 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1080/02640414.2019.1621476
ppbf_implication: Reinforces caution: PPBF should describe its youth policy as a reasoned position with stated uncertainty, not as evidence-based prescription.
verified_title: Youth sport specialization: a multidisciplinary scoping systematic review.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: A scoping review of 82 articles on multisport engagement in early athlete development found that different terms are used to describe the multisport pathway, most studies are empirical retrospective questionnaire studies aimed at the pathway to sporting excellence, and there is little investigation of when multisport engagement occurs or at what intensity.
effect_or_estimate: Definitional inconsistency; timing and intensity of multisport engagement under-investigated
limitations: Terminology heterogeneity is the finding.
citation: Is There Just One Type of Multisport Pathway? A Scoping Review of Multisport Engagement in Early Athlete Development. Sports Med Open 2023.
verification: pubmed:PMID 37851177 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1186/s40798-023-00644-x
ppbf_implication: If PPBF records multi-sport participation (recommended, see A3-062), it must define its own terms precisely and record dose, not just a yes/no flag.
verified_title: Is There Just One Type of Multisport Pathway? A Scoping Review of Multisport Engagement in Early Athlete Development.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: The IOC consensus statement on youth athletic development critically evaluated the state of science and practice and presented recommendations for developing healthy, resilient and capable youth athletes while providing opportunities for all levels of sport participation and success, challenging youth sport governing bodies to implement the guiding principles.
effect_or_estimate: Consensus principles
limitations: Consensus, 2015; principles rather than prescriptions.
citation: International Olympic Committee consensus statement on youth athletic development. Br J Sports Med 2015.
verification: pubmed:PMID 26084524 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1136/bjsports-2015-094962
ppbf_implication: The authoritative anchor for PPBF's youth development philosophy. Align PPBF's stated principles with it explicitly.
verified_title: International Olympic Committee consensus statement on youth athletic development.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: The 2024 IOC consensus statement on elite youth athletes competing at the Olympic Games notes adolescence is a vulnerable period of development that is inherently dynamic with non-linear and asynchronous progression of physical, physiological, psychological and social attributes, that age-based criteria and conventional pathways for youth Olympic candidates are not well or consistently defined, and that policies and practices vary widely across International Federations.
effect_or_estimate: Consensus position on non-linearity and inconsistent age criteria
limitations: Consensus; focused on the elite Olympic context, which most PPBF athletes will not enter.
citation: IOC consensus statement on elite youth athletes competing at the Olympic Games: essentials to a healthy, safe and sustainable paradigm. Br J Sports Med 2024.
verification: pubmed:PMID 39197945 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1136/bjsports-2024-108186
ppbf_implication: Any PPBF plan spanning a minor's growth period must surface maturation context rather than assume linear progression. Directly supports Module 109.
verified_title: IOC consensus statement on elite youth athletes competing at the Olympic Games: essentials to a healthy, safe and sustainable paradigm.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: A review of bio-banding - grouping youth athletes by maturity status, most commonly percentage of predicted young adult height, rather than chronological age - reports several applications in youth soccer with positive responses from players and coaches, and notes that bio-banding reduces but does not eliminate maturity-associated variation.
study_design: narrative review of concept and applications
effect_or_estimate: Reduces but does not eliminate maturity-associated variation
transfer_status: OTHER SPORT - soccer; boxing application untested
limitations: Predominantly male soccer; prediction of adult height carries its own error; no boxing studies.
citation: Bio-Banding in Youth Sports: Background, Concept, and Application. Sports Med 2019.
verification: pubmed:PMID 31429034 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1007/s40279-019-01166-x
ppbf_implication: In boxing, matching is governed by weight and age under the rulebooks, so bio-banding could only be a TRAINING-GROUP tool, never a matchmaking tool. PPBF cannot override governing-body matching rules.
verified_title: Bio-Banding in Youth Sports: Background, Concept, and Application.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: The National Strength and Conditioning Association updated position statement holds that research increasingly indicates resistance training can offer unique benefits for children and adolescents when appropriately prescribed and supervised, and that qualified acceptance of youth resistance training by medical, fitness and sport organisations is becoming universal.
effect_or_estimate: Categorical endorsement conditional on appropriate prescription and supervision
limitations: Position statement, 2009. 'Appropriately prescribed and supervised' is the load-bearing qualifier.
citation: Youth resistance training: updated position statement paper from the national strength and conditioning association. J Strength Cond Res 2009.
verification: pubmed:PMID 19620931 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1519/JSC.0b013e31819df407
ppbf_implication: Supervised youth resistance training is defensible in PPBF's youth stages. The supervision requirement is a coach-qualification requirement.
verified_title: Youth resistance training: updated position statement paper from the national strength and conditioning association.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: The 2014 International Consensus position statement on youth resistance training, adapted from the UK Strength and Conditioning Association position and endorsed by leading professional organisations across sports medicine, exercise science and paediatrics, supports youth resistance training.
effect_or_estimate: Categorical endorsement
limitations: Consensus, 2013/2014. A later audit found data informing governing-body resistance-training guidelines exhibit sex bias (Sports Med 2023).
citation: Position statement on youth resistance training: the 2014 International Consensus. Br J Sports Med 2013.
verification: pubmed:PMID 24055781 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1136/bjsports-2013-092952
ppbf_implication: Corroborates A3-072 with international endorsement. Note the sex-bias caveat when applying to female youth athletes.
verified_title: Position statement on youth resistance training: the 2014 International Consensus.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: A systematic review and meta-analysis found neuromuscular training injury prevention strategies are effective in youth sport.
effect_or_estimate: Effect sizes not extracted from the retrieved record - see the paper before quoting a number
limitations: Effect magnitude not extracted here; team-sport dominated; boxing-specific injury patterns (upper limb in training, head/neck in competition) differ.
citation: Neuromuscular training injury prevention strategies in youth sport: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Br J Sports Med 2015.
verification: pubmed:PMID 26084526 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1136/bjsports-2015-094639
ppbf_implication: Supports including a neuromuscular training component in PPBF's warm-up. Do not quote an effect size until the paper is read.
verified_title: Neuromuscular training injury prevention strategies in youth sport: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: A meta-analysis examined the dose-response relationship of neuromuscular training for injury prevention in youth athletes.
effect_or_estimate: Dose-response parameters not extracted from the retrieved record
limitations: Numbers not extracted; must be read before PPBF sets a neuromuscular training dose.
citation: Dose-Response Relationship of Neuromuscular Training for Injury Prevention in Youth Athletes: A Meta-Analysis. Front Physiol 2017.
verification: pubmed:PMID 29184511 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.3389/fphys.2017.00920
ppbf_implication: Read before prescribing a neuromuscular training dose. Do not invent one.
verified_title: Dose-Response Relationship of Neuromuscular Training for Injury Prevention in Youth Athletes: A Meta-Analysis.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: A meta-analysis of deliberate practice and performance across music, games, sports, education and professions found that deliberate practice explained a minority of the variance in performance.
effect_or_estimate: Deliberate practice explained a minority of performance variance
limitations: Contested by Ericsson and colleagues; the sport-specific companion analysis (PMID 27217246) is the more relevant one for PPBF.
citation: Deliberate practice and performance in music, games, sports, education, and professions: a meta-analysis. Psychol Sci 2014.
verification: pubmed:PMID 24986855 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1177/0956797614535810
ppbf_implication: Volume of structured practice matters but does not determine outcome. A development route must not imply that accumulating hours guarantees progression.
verified_title: Deliberate practice and performance in music, games, sports, education, and professions: a meta-analysis.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: A meta-analysis of the relationship between deliberate practice and performance specifically in sports was published in Perspectives on Psychological Science in 2016, alongside a published reply and commentary reflecting active scientific disagreement.
study_design: meta-analysis with published reply and commentary
effect_or_estimate: Effect magnitude not extracted; the existence of a formal published dispute is the recorded finding
limitations: An active academic dispute. PPBF should not adopt either extreme position.
citation: The Relationship Between Deliberate Practice and Performance in Sports: A Meta-Analysis. Perspect Psychol Sci 2016.
verification: pubmed:PMID 27217246 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1177/1745691616635591
ppbf_implication: Practice volume is one input among many. SHADOW should not treat accumulated hours as a progression criterion on its own.
verified_title: The Relationship Between Deliberate Practice and Performance in Sports: A Meta-Analysis.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: A meta-analysis of the contextual interference effect produced 139 effect-size estimates from 61 studies with an average overall effect size of 0.38, but with a significantly larger effect for basic research (0.57) than applied research (0.19), and for adults (0.50) than younger learners (0.10); the overall mean statistical power of the reviewed studies was 0.43.
competitive_level: mostly laboratory and applied practice contexts
effect_or_estimate: Overall d = 0.38; basic 0.57 vs applied 0.19; adults 0.50 vs younger learners 0.10; mean power 0.43
transfer_status: MOTOR LEARNING LABORATORY AND APPLIED - not boxing
limitations: Low mean statistical power (0.43) across the included studies. The applied effect (0.19) and the youth effect (0.10) are small.
citation: Contextual interference: a meta-analytic study. Percept Mot Skills 2004.
verification: pubmed:PMID 15446636 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.2466/pms.99.1.116-126
ppbf_implication: Interleaved practice is defensible for adult learners but the applied and youth effects are SMALL. Do not promise a large benefit from interleaving, and do not assume it transfers to children.
verified_title: Contextual interference: a meta-analytic study.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: An umbrella review of 12 systematic reviews and meta-analyses on small-sided games in team ball sports found positive effects on aerobic capacity and technical/tactical behaviours with more heterogeneous neuromuscular findings, but rated seven of the reviews low quality and five critically low quality using AMSTAR-2.
study_design: umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses
effect_or_estimate: Positive for aerobic capacity and technical/tactical behaviours; ALL 12 reviews rated low or critically low quality
limitations: The review-level evidence quality is poor by the authors' own AMSTAR-2 assessment.
citation: Small-sided games: An umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses. PLoS One 2021.
verification: pubmed:PMID 33577611 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0247067
ppbf_implication: Conditioned rounds with constraints (boxing's analogue of small-sided games) are reasonable practice, NOT proven practice. Present as coaching inference.
verified_title: Small-sided games: An umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: A systematic review and meta-analysis of tapering in endurance athletes (14 studies) found significant improvement from pre- to post-taper in time-trial performance (SMD -0.45) and time to exhaustion (SMD 1.28) with no significant improvement in VO2max or economy of movement; subgroup analysis found tapering combined with pre-taper overload had a greater effect than conventional tapering, and that reducing training volume by 41-60% while maintaining intensity and frequency, over durations of up to 7, 8-14 or 15-21 days using a progressive or step taper, significantly improved time-trial performance.
effect_or_estimate: Time trial SMD -0.45; TTE SMD 1.28; volume reduction 41-60% with intensity and frequency maintained
transfer_status: OTHER SPORT - ENDURANCE ATHLETES. No boxing taper trial was found.
limitations: Endurance performance outcomes, not combat-sport outcomes. Transfer to a technical, intermittent, weight-category combat sport is an assumption.
citation: Effects of tapering on performance in endurance athletes: A systematic review and meta-analysis. PLoS One 2023.
verification: pubmed:PMID 37163550 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0282838
ppbf_implication: The basis for PPBF's proposed taper template (40-60% volume reduction, intensity and frequency maintained, 7-14 days). MUST be labelled as transferred from endurance athletes and validated within PPBF.
verified_title: Effects of tapering on performance in endurance athletes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: A meta-analysis of the effects of tapering on performance examined 27 studies in competitive athletes against competition or field-based performance outcomes.
effect_or_estimate: Detailed parameter estimates not extracted from the retrieved record
limitations: 2007; parameters not extracted here. Read before quoting a taper duration from it.
citation: Effects of tapering on performance: a meta-analysis. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2007.
verification: pubmed:PMID 17762369 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1249/mss.0b013e31806010e0
ppbf_implication: Corroborates that tapering is one of the better-evidenced areas of periodisation. Read in full before PPBF finalises taper parameters.
verified_title: Effects of tapering on performance: a meta-analysis.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: In 21 elite judo athletes (10 international, 11 national) completing a 13-week block periodisation programme comprising a 5-week accumulation block, 5-week transmutation block and 3-week realisation block, Special Judo Fitness Test index improved from accumulation to transmutation in both groups with effect sizes of 0.83 (national) and 0.53 (international).
study_design: prospective observational study of a training block, no control group
effect_or_estimate: SJFT index improvement ES 0.83 (national) and 0.53 (international)
limitations: n=21, NO CONTROL GROUP, single programme. Cannot establish that block periodisation outperforms any alternative.
citation: Physiological and performance changes in national and international judo athletes during block periodization training. Biol Sport 2017.
verification: pubmed:PMID 29472740 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.5114/biolsport.2017.69825
ppbf_implication: The closest combat-sport evidence for a block model. It supports feasibility, not superiority. PPBF must not claim block periodisation is proven best.
verified_title: Physiological and performance changes in national and international judo athletes during block periodization training.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: A study comparing linear and daily undulating periodisation of strength training concurrent with judo training over 8 weeks in 13 adult male judo athletes (6 linear, 7 undulating) found strength improvements with both models.
study_design: randomised comparison of two periodisation models
effect_or_estimate: Both models improved strength; sample far too small to separate them
limitations: n=13 TOTAL. Severely underpowered to detect a difference between models. A null result here means nothing.
citation: Influence of linear and undulating strength periodization on physical fitness, physiological, and performance responses to simulated judo matches. J Strength Cond Res 2015.
verification: pubmed:PMID 24662235 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1519/JSC.0000000000000460
ppbf_implication: Do not choose between periodisation models on the basis of this evidence. There is no basis. PPBF should also NOT attempt its own model comparison - it will be underpowered too.
verified_title: Influence of linear and undulating strength periodization on physical fitness, physiological, and performance responses to simulated judo matches.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: A 2020 paper set out high-intensity interval training prescription for combat-sport athletes, including how to use combat-sport-specific parameters rather than generic running protocols.
effect_or_estimate: Prescription framework, not an effect estimate
limitations: A prescription framework by an expert author, not a trial of the framework itself.
citation: High-Intensity Interval Training Prescription for Combat-Sport Athletes. Int J Sports Physiol Perform 2020.
verification: pubmed:PMID 32502972 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1123/ijspp.2020-0289
ppbf_implication: Use to anchor HIIT prescription to boxing round structure and time-motion variables rather than to generic running protocols.
verified_title: High-Intensity Interval Training Prescription for Combat-Sport Athletes.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: A systematic review with meta-analysis of high-intensity interval training in combat sport athletes included 12 studies with 255 subjects and reported aerobic, anaerobic and anthropometric outcomes.
effect_or_estimate: Effect sizes not extracted from the retrieved record
boxing_specific: partly - combat sports including some boxing
limitations: Effect magnitudes not extracted; heterogeneous sports and protocols; small total sample.
citation: Effects of High-Intensity Interval Training in Combat Sports: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis. J Strength Cond Res 2020.
verification: pubmed:PMID 31904713 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1519/JSC.0000000000003255
ppbf_implication: Supports including HIIT in PPBF conditioning. Read the paper before quoting an effect size.
verified_title: Effects of High-Intensity Interval Training in Combat Sports: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: A separate systematic review examined the effects of high-intensity interval training on Olympic combat sports athletes' performance and physiological adaptation.
effect_or_estimate: Effect estimates not extracted from the retrieved record
limitations: Estimates not extracted here.
citation: Effects of High-Intensity Interval Training on Olympic Combat Sports Athletes' Performance and Physiological Adaptation: A Systematic Review. J Strength Cond Res 2019.
verification: pubmed:PMID 30431531 (metadata + abstract retrieved via PubMed MCP, 2026-08-07); DOI 10.1519/JSC.0000000000002957
ppbf_implication: Corroborating review. Read alongside A3-087 before setting HIIT parameters.
verified_title: Effects of High-Intensity Interval Training on Olympic Combat Sports Athletes' Performance and Physiological Adaptation: A Systematic Review.

track: Track 3 - Level/stage structures, regulatory pathway, session and annual/camp templates
claim: In 30 adolescent taekwondo athletes randomised to 20 s:10 s HIIT, 30 s:10 s HIIT or control over 8 weeks (24 sessions of 30 minutes), the 30 s:10 s group showed significantly greater improvement in VO2peak (4.72%) than the 20 s:10 s group (1.96%) or control (0.47%), while the 20 s:10 s group performed better on a short kick-frequency test and the 30 s group on longer sport-specific tests.
study_design: randomised controlled trial with three arms
effect_or_estimate: VO2peak improvement 4.72% (30:10) vs 1.96% (20:10) vs 0.47% (control)
transfer_status: OTHER COMBAT SPORT and ADOLESCENT population - transfer to boxing is a hypothesis
limitations: n=30 across three arms; taekwondo, not boxing; adolescents.

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Self-determination theory posits that satisfaction of autonomy, competence and relatedness underpins autonomous motivation and wellbeing; need frustration predicts ill-being. This is the theoretical spine, not a boxing finding.
effect_or_estimate: Theory statement; no single effect size
transfer_status: Non-boxing theory; applies as framework not as effect
limitations: Theory-level source; does not itself establish sport or boxing effects
citation: Ryan RM, Deci EL. Self-determination theory and the facilitation of intrinsic motivation, social development, and well-being. American Psychologist, 2000.
ppbf_implication: SHADOW motivation constructs (Module 071) should be modelled as three need-support signals rather than a single 'motivation score'.
verified_title: Self-determination theory and the facilitation of intrinsic motivation, social development, and well-being.

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Controlling coach behaviour and need thwarting form a distinct 'dark side' pathway associated with athlete ill-being, measurable separately from low need satisfaction.
effect_or_estimate: Psychometric structure supported; associations cross-sectional
transfer_status: Other-sport transfer to boxing; mechanism plausible, untested in boxing
limitations: Cross-sectional; self-report; causality not established
citation: Bartholomew KJ, Ntoumanis N, Ryan RM, Thøgersen-Ntoumani C. Psychological Need Thwarting in the Sport Context. Journal of Sport & Exercise Psychology, 2011.
ppbf_implication: PPBF must instrument coach behaviour negatively as well as positively; a 'no complaints' gym is not evidence of need support.
verified_title: Psychological Need Thwarting in the Sport Context: Assessing the Darker Side of Athletic Experience

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Meta-analytic evidence indicates SDT-informed interventions can change motivation and need satisfaction in health behaviour contexts; effects on distal behaviour are smaller and more variable.
effect_or_estimate: Direction favourable; magnitudes vary by outcome and are generally modest
transfer_status: Health-domain transfer; NOT boxing-specific and NOT youth-sport-specific
limitations: Health-domain, not sport-performance; heterogeneity; publication bias possible
citation: Ntoumanis N, Ng JYY, Prestwich A, Quested E, et al. A meta-analysis of self-determination theory-informed intervention studies in the health domain. Health Psychology Review, 2021.
ppbf_implication: Do not promise motivation gains in the app copy; frame as plausible mechanism with local measurement.
verified_title: A meta-analysis of self-determination theory-informed intervention studies in the health domain: effects on motivation, health behavior, physical, and psychological health

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Meta-analysis of autonomy-support intervention programmes (largely education) shows they can measurably increase autonomy-supportive behaviour in adults who lead others.
effect_or_estimate: Positive effects on autonomy-supportive behaviour reported
limitations: Predominantly educational settings; short follow-ups
citation: Su Y-L, Reeve J. A Meta-analysis of the Effectiveness of Intervention Programs Designed to Support Autonomy. Educational Psychology Review, 2011.
ppbf_implication: Coach-behaviour training is a defensible PPBF investment; effect on athlete outcomes must still be measured locally.
verified_title: A Meta-analysis of the Effectiveness of Intervention Programs Designed to Support Autonomy

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Controlling motivating style is partly situational and modifiable, not simply a fixed coach personality trait.
study_design: Conceptual review of experimental and field evidence
effect_or_estimate: No single estimate
limitations: Review, not primary trial; teacher not coach populations
citation: Reeve J. Why Teachers Adopt a Controlling Motivating Style Toward Students and How They Can Become More Autonomy Supportive. Educational Psychologist, 2009.
ppbf_implication: SHADOW coach-support prompts should target pressure sources (time, results, chaos) as well as coach phrasing.
verified_title: Why Teachers Adopt a Controlling Motivating Style Toward Students and How They Can Become More Autonomy Supportive

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: A motivational model of the coach–athlete relationship specifies autonomy-supportive behaviours (rationale, choice, acknowledging feelings, non-controlling feedback) as antecedents of athlete self-determined motivation.
effect_or_estimate: Model, not effect estimate
limitations: Model paper; predictions supported unevenly across later studies
citation: Mageau GA, Vallerand RJ. The coach-athlete relationship: a motivational model. Journal of Sports Sciences, 2003.
ppbf_implication: Provides the behaviour taxonomy for the PPBF coach behaviour library.
verified_title: The coach–athlete relationship: a motivational model

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Systematic review finds perceptions of a task-involving/mastery climate are associated with adaptive intrapersonal outcomes and ego-involving climate with maladaptive ones.
effect_or_estimate: Consistent direction of association; predominantly correlational
limitations: Mostly cross-sectional; climate usually athlete-perceived not observed
citation: Harwood CG, Keegan RJ, Smith JMJ, Raine AS. A systematic review of the intrapersonal correlates of motivational climate perceptions in sport and physical activity. Psychology of Sport and Exercise, 2015.
ppbf_implication: Climate is a gym-level variable PPBF can plausibly change; correlational status must be shown in the UI.
verified_title: A systematic review of the intrapersonal correlates of motivational climate perceptions in sport and physical activity

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: A coach-directed motivational climate intervention reduced young athletes' sport performance anxiety relative to control.
effect_or_estimate: Reduction in performance anxiety reported in intervention condition
transfer_status: Youth team-sport to youth boxing transfer; must be flagged
limitations: Single context; team sport; not replicated in combat sport
citation: Smith RE, Smoll FL, Cumming SP. Effects of a Motivational Climate Intervention for Coaches on Young Athletes' Sport Performance Anxiety. Journal of Sport & Exercise Psychology, 2007.
ppbf_implication: Strongest available warrant that coach-training changes youth athlete psychology; use as PPBF pilot template.
verified_title: Effects of a Motivational Climate Intervention for Coaches on Young Athletes’ Sport Performance Anxiety

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: The coach-created Empowering and Disempowering Motivational Climate Questionnaire (EDMCQ-C) provides an initially validated multi-dimensional climate measure integrating SDT and achievement goal constructs.
effect_or_estimate: Factor structure supported with noted limitations
limitations: Factor structure debated; measurement invariance work ongoing
citation: Appleton PR, Ntoumanis N, Quested E, Viladrich C, Duda JL. Initial validation of the coach-created Empowering and Disempowering Motivational Climate Questionnaire (EDMCQ-C). Psychology of Sport and Exercise, 2016.
ppbf_implication: Candidate PPBF climate instrument; requires local pilot before any scoring use.
verified_title: Initial validation of the coach-created Empowering and Disempowering Motivational Climate Questionnaire (EDMCQ-C)

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: The Empowering Coaching / PAPA programme provides a documented conceptual and empirical foundation for a large-scale coach-education climate intervention in grassroots youth sport.
population: Grassroots youth football coaches and players
effect_or_estimate: Programme design documented; effect claims must come from the trial reports, not the rationale paper
limitations: Rationale paper is not outcome evidence; effectiveness is mixed in later reports
citation: Duda JL. The conceptual and empirical foundations of Empowering Coaching: Setting the stage for the PAPA project. International Journal of Sport and Exercise Psychology, 2013.
ppbf_implication: Model for PPBF coach-education architecture; do not cite as proof of outcome change.
verified_title: The conceptual and empirical foundations of Empowering Coaching™: Setting the stage for the PAPA project

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Meta-analysis found a positive association between self-efficacy measures and sport performance; the relationship is moderated by measurement concordance and task type.
effect_or_estimate: Positive average association reported; magnitude varies with methodological concordance
transfer_status: Sport-general; includes lab and field tasks
limitations: Correlational core; reciprocal causation with prior performance is likely
citation: Moritz SE, Feltz DL, Fahrbach KR, Mack DE. The Relation of Self-Efficacy Measures to Sport Performance: A Meta-Analytic Review. Research Quarterly for Exercise and Sport, 2000.
ppbf_implication: Confidence Stability Engine (Module 066) must model past performance as a confound, not treat confidence as an independent driver.
verified_title: The Relation of Self-Efficacy Measures to Sport Performance: A Meta-Analytic Review

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Sport-confidence has been conceptualised and instrumented as multi-source (mastery, demonstration of ability, physical/mental preparation, social support, coach leadership, and others).
effect_or_estimate: Source structure supported
limitations: Older instrumentation; sources may not be equally salient in combat sport
citation: Vealey RS, Hayashi SW, Garner-Holman M, Giacobbi P. Sources of Sport-Confidence: Conceptualization and Instrument Development. Journal of Sport and Exercise Psychology, 1998.
ppbf_implication: Confidence in SHADOW should be attributed to a source, enabling a coach to act, rather than reported as a bare number.
verified_title: Sources of Sport-Confidence: Conceptualization and Instrument Development

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: A grounded theory of psychological resilience in Olympic champions describes protective psychological factors that influence appraisal and meta-cognition under stress.
effect_or_estimate: Theory, not effect estimate
transfer_status: Elite-to-youth transfer is NOT supported by this study
limitations: Retrospective interviews with successful athletes only; survivorship bias; no failure comparison group
citation: Fletcher D, Sarkar M. A grounded theory of psychological resilience in Olympic champions. Psychology of Sport and Exercise, 2012.
ppbf_implication: Do NOT use elite-champion resilience profiles as a youth development target in PPBF.
verified_title: A grounded theory of psychological resilience in Olympic champions

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Systematic review across sport and work domains finds resilience is inconsistently defined and operationalised, limiting cross-study comparison.
effect_or_estimate: Definitional heterogeneity documented
limitations: Construct proliferation; measurement not interchangeable
citation: Bryan C, O'Shea D, MacIntyre T. Stressing the relevance of resilience: a systematic review of resilience across the domains of sport and work. International Review of Sport and Exercise Psychology, 2019.
ppbf_implication: PPBF must not ship a single 'resilience score'; specify the operational definition or use a behavioural proxy.
verified_title: Stressing the relevance of resilience: a systematic review of resilience across the domains of sport and work

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: The Individual Zones of Optimal Functioning model holds that the emotion intensity associated with best performance is individual-specific rather than a common optimum.
effect_or_estimate: Individual-specific zones supported in small samples
limitations: Idiographic method; predictive validity across seasons under-tested
source_type: Authoritative text chapter / peer-reviewed applied studies
citation: Hanin YL. Individual Zones of Optimal Functioning (IZOF) Model. In: Emotions in Sport, 2000; and Hanin YL, Syrjä P. Performance Affect in Junior Ice Hockey Players. The Sport Psychologist, 1995.
ppbf_implication: SHADOW must NOT apply a population arousal threshold; any arousal-performance link must be built per athlete.
verified_title: Individual Zones of Optimal Functioning (IZOF) Model

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Catastrophe models predict that under high cognitive anxiety, increasing physiological arousal can produce a sudden rather than gradual performance drop, with hysteresis on recovery.
effect_or_estimate: Support is mixed across tests
limitations: Difficult to test; results inconsistent; parameter estimation contested
citation: Hardy L. Testing the Predictions of the Cusp Catastrophe Model of Anxiety and Performance. The Sport Psychologist, 1996; Hardy L, Parfitt G. A catastrophe model of anxiety and performance. British Journal of Psychology, 1991.
ppbf_implication: Justifies treating a boxer's 'sudden fall-apart round' as plausible, but PPBF cannot predict it from an anxiety score.
verified_title: Testing the Predictions of the Cusp Catastrophe Model of Anxiety and Performance

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Anxiety symptoms carry a directional dimension (facilitative vs debilitative interpretation) that adds explanatory value beyond intensity alone.
effect_or_estimate: Direction adds variance beyond intensity
limitations: Self-report; direction scales debated; cross-sectional
citation: Jones G, Swain A. Intensity and Direction as Dimensions of Competitive State Anxiety and Relationships with Competitiveness. Perceptual and Motor Skills, 1992; Jones G, Swain A, Hardy L. Journal of Sports Sciences, 1993.
ppbf_implication: If PPBF ever collects pre-bout nerves, it must capture interpretation ('helpful/unhelpful'), not intensity alone.
verified_title: Intensity and Direction as Dimensions of Competitive State Anxiety and Relationships with Competitiveness

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Attentional control theory proposes anxiety impairs efficiency of the goal-directed attentional system and increases stimulus-driven attention, degrading processing efficiency before it degrades effectiveness.
effect_or_estimate: Robust in cognitive tasks
transfer_status: LAB EVIDENCE — transfer to boxing decision-making is inference, not demonstration
limitations: Cognitive laboratory tasks; sport application requires separate evidence
citation: Eysenck MW, Derakshan N, Santos R, Calvo MG. Anxiety and cognitive performance: Attentional control theory. Emotion, 2007.
ppbf_implication: Explains why an anxious boxer may look 'the same but slower to read'; supports effort/efficiency coach prompts.
verified_title: Anxiety and cognitive performance: Attentional control theory.

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
topic: Anxiety — anxiety determinants in elite athletes
claim: Systematic review and meta-analysis identified determinants of anxiety in elite athletes across individual and contextual factors.
effect_or_estimate: Determinants identified; heterogeneity present
limitations: Elite samples; limited female-specific and combat-sport-specific breakdown
citation: Rice SM, Gwyther K, Santesteban-Echarri O, et al. Determinants of anxiety in elite athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis. British Journal of Sports Medicine, 2019.
ppbf_implication: Do not extrapolate elite anxiety determinants to PPBF novices without local checking.
verified_title: Determinants of anxiety in elite athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Skills learned with more explicit knowledge are more prone to breakdown under pressure than skills learned implicitly; conscious re-processing of automated movement is a candidate mechanism.
population: Adult novices (golf putting) and later replications
effect_or_estimate: Explicit-learning groups degraded more under pressure
transfer_status: LAB / closed-skill task — boxing is open-skill; transfer is inference
limitations: Closed-skill laboratory task; novices; not combat-sport validated
citation: Masters RSW. Knowledge, knerves and know-how. British Journal of Psychology, 1992.
ppbf_implication: Argues against over-verbalising technical cues immediately before pressured performance in the PPBF cue library.
verified_title: Knowledge, knerves and know‐how: The role of explicit versus implicit knowledge in the breakdown of a complex motor skill under pressure
title_consistency_check: MANUALLY REVIEWED — author-year or multi-source citation, record confirmed

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Experimental work supports skill-focused attention (self-focus/execution-focus) as a mechanism of choking in proceduralised skills.
effect_or_estimate: Skill-focus manipulation degraded proceduralised performance
transfer_status: LAB — open-skill combat transfer is inference
limitations: Lab tasks; not fight conditions
citation: Beilock SL, Carr TH. On the fragility of skilled performance: What governs choking under pressure? Journal of Experimental Psychology: General, 2001.
ppbf_implication: Supports external-focus / holistic cueing in high-pressure rounds; label as inference from lab work.
verified_title: On the fragility of skilled performance: What governs choking under pressure?

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Systematic review of choking interventions in sport reports some support for pre-performance routines, quiet eye and analogy/implicit approaches, but with small samples and design limitations.
effect_or_estimate: Direction favourable; evidence quality limited
limitations: Small samples; heterogeneous pressure manipulations; limited retention data
citation: Gröpel P, Mesagno C. Choking interventions in sports: A systematic review. International Review of Sport and Exercise Psychology, 2019.
ppbf_implication: PPBF may pilot pre-performance routines; must not claim a proven anti-choking protocol.
verified_title: Choking interventions in sports: A systematic review

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Meta-analysis of pre-performance routines reports a positive overall effect on sport performance.
effect_or_estimate: Positive pooled effect reported
transfer_status: Predominantly self-paced/closed skills; boxing is externally paced — transfer flagged
limitations: Dominated by closed-skill tasks (golf, shooting, free throws); externally paced combat application unverified
citation: Rupprecht ADP, Tran US, Gröpel P. The effectiveness of pre-performance routines in sports: a meta-analysis. International Review of Sport and Exercise Psychology, 2021.
ppbf_implication: Routine support is defensible for glove-up / corner rituals; effect size cannot be assumed to carry to open-skill exchanges.
verified_title: The effectiveness of pre-performance routines in sports: a meta-analysis

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: A comparison of different pre-performance routines found routine content and structure influence outcomes in choking-susceptible athletes.
effect_or_estimate: Differences between routine types reported
limitations: Small sample; single laboratory-style context
citation: Mesagno C, Mullane-Grant T. A Comparison of Different Pre-Performance Routines as Possible Choking Interventions. Journal of Applied Sport Psychology, 2010.
ppbf_implication: Routine content should be athlete-authored and logged, not templated by SHADOW.
verified_title: A Comparison of Different Pre-Performance Routines as Possible Choking Interventions

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Review of self-talk research supports performance benefits, with moderators including task type (fine vs gross), self-talk content (instructional vs motivational), and training of the technique.
effect_or_estimate: Benefit reported; moderated by task and content
limitations: Many small studies; acute performance outcomes dominate; retention/transfer under-reported
citation: Hatzigeorgiadis A, Zourbanos N, Galanis E, Theodorakis Y. Self-Talk and Sports Performance: A Meta-Analysis. Perspectives on Psychological Science, 2011.
ppbf_implication: Instructional self-talk fits novel technical work; motivational self-talk fits effort/conditioning — encode this split in the cue library.
verified_title: Self-Talk and Sports Performance

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Meta-analysis of imagery interventions in sport reports positive effects on performance, moderated by imagery type and intervention characteristics.
effect_or_estimate: Positive pooled effect reported
limitations: Heterogeneous protocols; short follow-up; risk of publication bias
citation: Simonsmeier BA, Andronie M, Buecker S, Frank C. The effects of imagery interventions in sports: a meta-analysis. International Review of Sport and Exercise Psychology, 2021.
ppbf_implication: Imagery is a low-risk, coach-deliverable homework candidate for Module 092; measure adherence not just assignment.
verified_title: The effects of imagery interventions in sports: a meta-analysis

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Meta-analysis of psychological and psychosocial interventions reports overall positive effects on sport performance.
effect_or_estimate: Positive pooled effect on performance
limitations: Heterogeneous interventions and outcomes; many small studies
citation: Brown DJ, Fletcher D. Effects of Psychological and Psychosocial Interventions on Sport Performance: A Meta-Analysis. Sports Medicine, 2017.
ppbf_implication: Supports a PST lane in PPBF but not any specific dose; dose is TBD locally.
verified_title: Effects of Psychological and Psychosocial Interventions on Sport Performance: A Meta-Analysis

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: A systematic review of sport-psychology performance meta-analyses maps the evidence base and its methodological quality across constructs.
effect_or_estimate: Quality and coverage vary substantially by construct
limitations: Umbrella review inherits primary-study limitations
citation: Lochbaum M, Stoner E, Hefner T, Cooper S, Lane AM, Terry PC. Sport psychology and performance meta-analyses: A systematic review of the literature. PLOS ONE, 2022.
ppbf_implication: Use as the PPBF triage map for which psych constructs have defensible evidence at all.
verified_title: Sport psychology and performance meta-analyses: A systematic review of the literature

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Meta-analysis reports longer quiet-eye durations in experts and in successful performance attempts.
effect_or_estimate: Expert and successful-trial advantage reported
transfer_status: Predominantly aiming/interceptive tasks; boxing gaze evidence is sparse — flagged as transfer
limitations: Dominated by targeting tasks; causal training effects less established than correlational differences
citation: Lebeau J-C, Liu S, Sáenz-Moncaleano C, et al. Quiet Eye and Performance in Sport: A Meta-Analysis. Journal of Sport and Exercise Psychology, 2016.
ppbf_implication: Attention Control Engine (Module 059) must not import quiet-eye thresholds from golf/shooting into boxing.
verified_title: Quiet Eye and Performance in Sport: A Meta-Analysis

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
topic: Fatigue — mental fatigue and physical performance
claim: Systematic review reports mental fatigue impairs endurance performance while leaving maximal strength/power largely unaffected.
effect_or_estimate: Endurance impaired; maximal strength/power broadly unaffected
limitations: Lab fatigue protocols; ecological validity limited
citation: Van Cutsem J, Marcora S, De Pauw K, Bailey S, Meeusen R, Roelands B. The Effects of Mental Fatigue on Physical Performance: A Systematic Review. Sports Medicine, 2017.
ppbf_implication: Session ordering matters: heavy cognitive load before conditioning is a plausible confounder in PPBF session outcome data.
verified_title: The Effects of Mental Fatigue on Physical Performance: A Systematic Review

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
topic: Fatigue — mental fatigue and skilled performance
claim: Systematic review reports mental fatigue can impair sport-specific skilled and decision-making performance, though effects vary by task and induction protocol.
effect_or_estimate: Impairment reported across several skill domains; heterogeneity present
limitations: Heterogeneous fatigue inductions; small samples; some null findings
citation: Habay J, Van Cutsem J, Verschueren J, et al. Does mental fatigue affect skilled performance in athletes? A systematic review. PLOS ONE, 2021.
ppbf_implication: Decision-Making Engine (Module 057) should record cognitive load context before scoring a decision error.
verified_title: Does mental fatigue affect skilled performance in athletes? A systematic review

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Systematic review and meta-analysis reports goal setting has performance and psychological effects in sport, with moderators and notable methodological limitations in the primary literature.
effect_or_estimate: Positive effects reported with moderation and quality caveats
limitations: Primary study quality variable; goal fidelity often unmeasured
citation: Williamson O, Swann C, Bennett KJM, et al. The performance and psychological effects of goal setting in sport: A systematic review and meta-analysis. International Review of Sport and Exercise Psychology, 2022.
ppbf_implication: Goal Management System (Module 011) has evidential warrant to exist; specific goal templates do not.
verified_title: The performance and psychological effects of goal setting in sport: A systematic review and meta-analysis

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
topic: Goal setting — applied critique of SMART
claim: Applied review of goal setting in sport psychology practice critiques mechanical SMART-goal prescription and argues for a process-oriented, athlete-involved, revisable goal process including open goals in some contexts.
effect_or_estimate: Critique, not effect estimate
limitations: Review of practice; not a controlled comparison of SMART vs alternatives
citation: Bird MD, Swann C, Jackman PC. The what, why, and how of goal setting: A review of the goal-setting process in applied sport psychology practice. Journal of Applied Sport Psychology, 2024.
ppbf_implication: PPBF goal intake must capture the athlete's own words and 'why', permit revision, and avoid auto-generating SMART strings.
verified_title: The what, why, and how of goal setting: A review of the goal-setting process in applied sport psychology practice

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Systematic review of Goal Setting Theory application to sport interventions finds inconsistent fidelity to the theory in sport goal-setting studies.
effect_or_estimate: Fidelity gaps documented
limitations: Review of implementation quality, not of outcome magnitude
citation: Jeong YH, Healy LC, McEwan D. The application of Goal Setting Theory to goal setting interventions in sport: a systematic review. International Review of Sport and Exercise Psychology, 2023.
ppbf_implication: PPBF should log goal fidelity attributes (specificity, difficulty, commitment, feedback) as fields, enabling later audit.
verified_title: The application of Goal Setting Theory to goal setting interventions in sport: a systematic review

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Influential critique argues over-prescribed goal setting can produce systematic side effects including narrowed focus, unethical behaviour, risk distortion and reduced intrinsic motivation.
effect_or_estimate: No pooled estimate; contested by goal-setting theorists
transfer_status: MANAGEMENT-domain transfer; explicitly not a sport finding
limitations: Contested; rebutted by Locke & Latham; case-based reasoning
citation: Ordóñez LD, Schweitzer ME, Galinsky AD, Bazerman MH. Goals Gone Wild: The Systematic Side Effects of Overprescribing Goal Setting. Academy of Management Perspectives, 2009.
ppbf_implication: Warrants a PPBF guardrail: outcome goals tied to bout results must not be auto-assigned to youth.
verified_title: Goals Gone Wild: The Systematic Side Effects of Overprescribing Goal Setting

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Goal Setting Theory holds that specific difficult goals produce higher performance than vague or easy goals, mediated by effort, persistence, direction and strategy, and moderated by commitment, feedback and task complexity.
study_design: Theory synthesis of a large empirical programme
effect_or_estimate: Robust in work/lab settings
transfer_status: WORK/LAB origin; sport application requires sport evidence (see A4-032)
limitations: Task complexity attenuates effects; sport is high in complexity
citation: Locke EA, Latham GP. Building a practically useful theory of goal setting and task motivation: A 35-year odyssey. American Psychologist, 2002.
ppbf_implication: Feedback is a named moderator — a PPBF goal without a feedback loop is theoretically expected to underperform.
verified_title: Building a practically useful theory of goal setting and task motivation: A 35-year odyssey.

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: The Athletic Identity Measurement Scale is the dominant instrument for athletic identity; a systematic review with meta-analysis has examined its properties across three decades.
study_design: Systematic review with meta-analysis of a scale
effect_or_estimate: Psychometric findings synthesised; factor structure debated across versions
limitations: Version proliferation; cross-cultural invariance incomplete
citation: Costa S, et al. The Athletic Identity Measurement Scale: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis from 1993 to 2021. European Journal of Investigation in Health, Psychology and Education, 2022.
ppbf_implication: If PPBF measures identity it must use a named version and store version metadata; identity is privacy-sensitive.
verified_title: The Athletic Identity Measurement Scale: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis from 1993 to 2021

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Systematic literature review of academic and athletic identities in student-athletes documents tension between athletic identity strength and broader identity/career exploration.
effect_or_estimate: Associations documented; causal direction unresolved
transfer_status: US collegiate context; NOT directly a community youth-boxing finding
limitations: Predominantly US collegiate; cross-sectional dominance
citation: Steele AR, van Rens FECA, Ashley R. A Systematic Literature Review on the Academic and Athletic Identities of Student-Athletes. Journal of Intercollegiate Sport, 2020.
verification: openalex:W3082256575 (record returned by OpenAlex search); crossref DOI resolved
ppbf_implication: Supports a PPBF 'life beyond boxing' pathway; do not present identity foreclosure as diagnosed in any athlete.
verified_title: A Systematic Literature Review on the Academic and Athletic Identities of Student-Athletes

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Systematic review of athletes' career transition out of sport identifies quality-of-transition factors including identity, preparation and support.
effect_or_estimate: Factors identified; heterogeneous methods
limitations: Retrospective designs common
citation: Park S, Lavallee D, Tod D. Athletes' career transition out of sport: a systematic review. International Review of Sport and Exercise Psychology, 2013.

ppbf_implication: Relevant to PPBF alumni and to athletes who stop boxing; supports exit-interview data capture.
verified_title: Athletes' career transition out of sport: a systematic review

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: The Athlete Burnout Questionnaire operationalises burnout as emotional/physical exhaustion, reduced sense of accomplishment, and sport devaluation.
effect_or_estimate: Three-factor structure supported

ppbf_implication: PPBF may track the three dimensions descriptively; SHADOW must not label an athlete 'burned out'.
verified_title: Development and Preliminary Validation of an Athlete Burnout Measure

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Systematic review of burnout in sport synthesises antecedents including training load, motivational profile, perfectionism and social environment.

verified_title: Burnout in Sport: A Systematic Review

track: A4 Psychology / Human Development / Life-Skill Transfer
claim: Longitudinal study of young elite handball players links athlete burnout to subsequent dropout risk.
effect_or_estimate: Burnout associated with dropout risk

citation: Isoard-Gautheur S, Guillet-Descas E, Gustafsson H. Athlete Burnout and the Risk of Dropout Among Young Elite Handball Players. The Sport Psychologist, 2016.
