track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: The National Athletic Trainers' Association published a position statement on safe weight loss and maintenance practices in sport and exercise, providing recommendations for athletic trainers and guidance for athletes, coaches and parents, and identifying fluid restriction and pathogenic weight-control behaviours as unsafe practices.
effect_or_estimate: Qualitative recommendations; no single numeric rate endorsed in the abstract
limitations: 2011 statement; addressed primarily to athletic trainers, a role PPBF may not staff; recommendations require a qualified professional to apply
citation: Turocy PS, et al. National Athletic Trainers' Association position statement: safe weight loss and maintenance practices in sport and exercise. J Athl Train. 2011.
ppbf_implication: PPBF should name which qualified human holds this role locally; if no athletic trainer is on staff, the referral goes to the athlete's physician.
verified_title: National Athletic Trainers' Association position statement: safe weight loss and maintenance practices in sport and exercise.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: The American Academy of Pediatrics has published both a policy statement (2005) and a clinical report (2017) describing unhealthy weight-loss and weight-gain methods in young athletes, including in weight-class sports such as wrestling and martial arts, and providing recommendations for paediatricians on discouraging inappropriate weight-control behaviours.
study_design: Professional-body policy statement and clinical report
effect_or_estimate: Qualitative; the documents describe unhealthy practices and recommend they be discouraged
boxing_specific: No — general youth sport, explicitly including weight-class sports
transfer_status: Direct paediatric authority applicable to PPBF's youth lane
limitations: Guidance is addressed to paediatricians, not to coaches or software; the 2005 policy statement is superseded in practice by the 2017 clinical report
citation: American Academy of Pediatrics. Promotion of healthy weight-control practices in young athletes. Pediatrics. 2005; and Promotion of Healthy Weight-Control Practices in Young Athletes. Pediatrics. 2017 (clinical report).
ppbf_implication: Together with the youth weight-cycling systematic review, this is the professional-body basis for PPBF's categorical youth prohibition.
verified_title: Promotion of healthy weight-control practices in young athletes.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: The 2025 ISSN position stand on combat sports states that post-weigh-in oral rehydration solutions of 1 to 1.5 litres per hour with sodium in the 50-90 mmol range should take precedence, followed by fast-acting carbohydrate at up to 60 g/h, and that protocols should aim to regain at least 10% of body mass; the same statement acknowledges that the long-term effects of frequent weight cuts on health and performance are unknown.
population: Combat-sport athletes, primarily MMA and day-before-weigh-in sports
effect_or_estimate: ORS 1-1.5 L/h with 50-90 mmol sodium; carbohydrate <=60 g/h; post-weigh-in carbohydrate 8-12 g/kg after significant depletion or 4-7 g/kg after modest restriction; target regain >=10% body mass
transfer_status: Combat-sport evidence; the recovery protocols assume a day-before weigh-in with hours of recovery, which does not exist in same-day amateur boxing
limitations: This position stand also describes acute water-loss methods (sauna, hot water immersion, mummy wraps, water loading, sodium restriction) that PPBF prohibits; PPBF's disagreement is a governance choice about a youth-serving community programme, not a claim that the position stand is wrong for supervised professional MMA. The stand itself states the long-term health effects are unknown, and its recovery protocols are irrelevant to a same-day weigh-in
citation: Jagim AR, et al. International society of sports nutrition position stand: nutrition and weight cut strategies for mixed martial arts and other combat sports. J Int Soc Sports Nutr. 2025.
verification: pubmed:PMID 40059405 (metadata + full abstract with all 16 position points retrieved)
ppbf_implication: MAJOR CONFLICT FOR SYNTHESIS: a current ISSN position stand describes weight-cut methods PPBF prohibits. PPBF must state explicitly that it declines to implement those sections for a youth-serving community programme and why.
verified_title: International society of sports nutrition position stand: nutrition and weight cut strategies for mixed martial arts and other combat sports.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: A prospective study has evaluated a structured weight management protocol as an alternative to rapid weight loss in mixed martial arts, indicating that alternatives to acute cutting are being formally tested.
effect_or_estimate: Effect estimates not extracted from the abstract
limitations: Single study; MMA; no boxing replication; a structured alternative protocol is not yet an evidence-based standard
citation: An alternative structured weight management protocol to rapid weight loss in mixed martial arts: a prospective study. Front Nutr. 2025.
ppbf_implication: Supports PPBF's position that a longitudinal, supervised descent is a testable alternative rather than an untried idea.
verified_title: An alternative structured weight management protocol to rapid weight loss in mixed martial arts: a prospective interventional study of pre-competition weight management strategies in professional athletes.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: The Female Athlete Triad comprises low energy availability with or without disordered eating, menstrual dysfunction, and low bone mineral density; the 2014 Coalition consensus provides screening, diagnosis, treatment and return-to-play guidance for physicians and healthcare providers. A parallel Male Athlete Triad consensus was published in 2021.
population: Physically active girls and women; and male athletes for the parallel statement
effect_or_estimate: Three-component construct; clinical guidance rather than numeric thresholds for app use
limitations: Return-to-play decisions under these statements are explicitly clinical; the Triad framework and the newer REDs framework overlap and are not fully reconciled in the literature
citation: De Souza MJ, et al. 2014 Female Athlete Triad Coalition Consensus Statement on Treatment and Return to Play. Br J Sports Med. 2014; Nattiv A, et al. The Male Athlete Triad - Part II. Clin J Sport Med. 2021.
ppbf_implication: Return-to-play under a Triad diagnosis is a physician decision; SHADOW may hold the administrative status flag only.
verified_title: 2014 Female Athlete Triad Coalition Consensus Statement on Treatment and Return to Play of the Female Athlete Triad: 1st International Conference held in San Francisco, California, May 2012 and 2nd International Conference held in Indianapolis, Indiana, May 2013.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: The ISSN position stand on the female athlete states that female athletes have unique hormone profiles influencing physiology and nutritional needs across the lifespan and recommends that athletes of reproductive age track hormonal status against training and recovery to determine individual patterns.
effect_or_estimate: Recommends individual tracking rather than a population prescription
limitations: The female-athlete evidence base is substantially smaller than the male base across most nutrition topics; menstrual-cycle-phase nutrition recommendations remain largely hypothesis-level
citation: Sims ST, et al. International society of sports nutrition position stand: nutritional concerns of the female athlete. J Int Soc Sports Nutr. 2023.
ppbf_implication: Menstrual-cycle data is special-category health data; PPBF must treat any tracking as opt-in, privacy-tiered, and never coach-visible by default.
verified_title: International society of sports nutrition position stand: nutritional concerns of the female athlete.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: Amenorrhoea in adolescent female athletes should not be considered normal; low energy availability is a common cause, and because adolescence is a critical period for bone accrual, delayed menarche and secondary amenorrhoea are of particular concern in young athletes.
study_design: Peer-reviewed review in a paediatric journal
effect_or_estimate: Qualitative clinical position; no app-usable numeric threshold
limitations: Review, not a trial; causal attribution of amenorrhoea to LEA in an individual requires clinical exclusion of other causes
citation: Amenorrhoea in adolescent female athletes. Lancet Child Adolesc Health. 2018.
ppbf_implication: Amenorrhoea reported by a PPBF adolescent athlete is a physician referral with no coach-side interpretation.
verified_title: Amenorrhoea in adolescent female athletes.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: Adolescent, female and masters athletes have distinct nutritional requirements arising from age- and sex-related physiological changes in addition to training demands, with education focused on long-term health and on at-risk dietary patterns including sustained restricted eating and low calcium, vitamin D or iron intakes.
study_design: Review in a sports nutrition journal
effect_or_estimate: Qualitative; identifies at-risk patterns rather than numeric targets
limitations: Narrative review; each of the three populations is under-researched relative to adult male athletes
citation: Desbrow B, et al. Nutrition for Special Populations: Young, Female, and Masters Athletes. Int J Sport Nutr Exerc Metab. 2019.
ppbf_implication: Provides the structure for PPBF's age- and sex-banded education content across youth, female and masters lanes.
verified_title: Nutrition for Special Populations: Young, Female, and Masters Athletes.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: Contrary to earlier thinking, youth do not have less effective thermoregulatory ability, insufficient cardiovascular capacity, or lower exertion tolerance than adults when exercising in the heat provided adequate hydration is maintained; the primary determinants of reduced performance and exertional heat-illness risk in youth are poor hydration status, undue exertion, and insufficient recovery between repeated bouts.
effect_or_estimate: Qualitative; identifies hydration status, exertion and recovery as the primary determinants
limitations: 2011 statement; concerns environmental heat exposure generally rather than deliberate heat exposure for weight making
citation: American Academy of Pediatrics Council on Sports Medicine and Fitness and Council on School Health. Policy statement - Climatic heat stress and exercising children and adolescents. Pediatrics. 2011.
ppbf_implication: Directly contradicts any use of sauna, hot rooms or impermeable suits with minors at PPBF; deliberate hydration compromise removes the very protection this statement depends on.
verified_title: Policy statement—Climatic heat stress and exercising children and adolescents.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: The IOC REDs body-composition subgroup found that higher body fat was negatively associated with endurance performance and that muscle-mass gain benefited performance across sports, but that body composition did not contribute to talent identification and no unique cut-off signifying a performance advantage was identified; body composition is one of many variables and its influence should not be overstated.
study_design: Critical review of 29 longitudinal, prospective or intervention studies plus an international practitioner survey
effect_or_estimate: No unique body-composition cut-off identified as conferring a performance advantage
limitations: Association is not causation; the review explicitly cautions against overstating body composition's role; the survey component reflects current practice rather than evidence
citation: Ackerman KE, et al. Best practice recommendations for body composition considerations in sport to reduce health and performance risks: a critical review, original survey and expert opinion by a subgroup of the IOC consensus on REDs. Br J Sports Med. 2023.
ppbf_implication: PPBF must not display a body-fat target or a leanness ranking to any athlete; no cut-off exists to justify one.
verified_title: Best practice recommendations for body composition considerations in sport to reduce health and performance risks: a critical review, original survey and expert opinion by a subgroup of the IOC consensus on Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs).

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: Interpreting body-composition change requires the least significant change concept; same-day consecutive DXA scans capture technical error only, while consecutive-day scans additionally capture short-term biological variation, which is the relevant error term for longitudinal monitoring.
effect_or_estimate: Least significant change differs between same-day and consecutive-day protocols; the consecutive-day estimate is larger
limitations: DXA-specific; site- and machine-specific; PPBF is unlikely to have DXA access, so the practical error term for whatever method PPBF uses is unmeasured
citation: Same-Day Vs Consecutive-Day Precision Error of Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry for Interpreting Body Composition Change in Resistance-Trained Athletes. J Clin Densitom. 2018.
ppbf_implication: Any PPBF body-composition trend line must carry a measurement-error band; PPBF's own least significant change is TBD and must be measured before trends are displayed.
verified_title: Same-Day Vs Consecutive-Day Precision Error of Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry for Interpreting Body Composition Change in Resistance-Trained Athletes.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: Bioelectrical impedance vector analysis has been systematically reviewed for use in sport and exercise, covering body composition, hydration status and related characteristics; hydration status is itself a determinant of impedance-based estimates.
effect_or_estimate: Qualitative synthesis; no single validated accuracy figure applicable across devices
limitations: Impedance measures are confounded by hydration status, which is precisely the variable that is disturbed in a weight-cutting athlete; consumer body-fat scales are the least accurate implementation
citation: Castizo-Olier J, et al. Bioelectrical impedance vector analysis (BIVA) in sport and exercise: Systematic review and future perspectives. PLoS One. 2018.
ppbf_implication: A consumer impedance scale in a boxing gym will read an athlete's dehydration as fat loss; PPBF should not use one for body-composition decisions.
verified_title: Bioelectrical impedance vector analysis (BIVA) in sport and exercise: Systematic review and future perspectives.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: Exercise-induced gastrointestinal syndrome and exercise-associated gastrointestinal symptoms are common in endurance athletes; a systematic review examined whether repeated exposure of the gut to nutrients before and during exercise ('gut training') improves gastrointestinal integrity, function and symptoms.
study_design: Systematic literature review across five databases
effect_or_estimate: Qualitative synthesis; gut-training protocols vary widely
transfer_status: Endurance transfer; no boxing-specific gut-training evidence located
limitations: Endurance-derived; the practical relevance to a 3x3 min bout is limited, but the principle of rehearsing competition-day feeding in training does transfer
citation: The Effect of Gut-Training and Feeding-Challenge on Markers of Gastrointestinal Status in Response to Endurance Exercise: A Systematic Literature Review. Sports Med. 2023.
ppbf_implication: PPBF's practical rule is 'nothing new on competition day', rehearsed in training - the transferable principle without the endurance intake volumes.
verified_title: The Effect of Gut-Training and Feeding-Challenge on Markers of Gastrointestinal Status in Response to Endurance Exercise: A Systematic Literature Review.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: A systematic review of randomised trials examined the effect of probiotic supplementation on gastrointestinal symptoms in athletes.
study_design: Systematic review of randomised controlled trials
effect_or_estimate: No clear consistent benefit extractable; strains, doses and outcome measures are heterogeneous
limitations: Probiotic strain specificity means results do not generalise across products; no boxing evidence; commercial products are a cost burden with unproven benefit
citation: Effects of Probiotics Supplementation on Gastrointestinal Symptoms in Athletes: A Systematic Review of Randomised Controlled Trials. Nutrients. 2022.
ppbf_implication: PPBF should not recommend probiotics; the cost is real and the benefit is unestablished.
verified_title: Effects of Probiotics Supplementation on Gastrointestinal Symptoms in Athletes: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: Co-ingestion of protein with carbohydrate after exercise has been examined for its effect on muscle glycogen restoration and functional capacity; a separate systematic review assessed whether carbohydrate with protein increases the rate of muscle glycogen resynthesis compared with carbohydrate alone.
effect_or_estimate: Benefit of adding protein is most apparent when carbohydrate intake is sub-optimal; at adequate carbohydrate intakes the additional glycogen effect diminishes
limitations: Glycogen resynthesis rate is a surrogate for recovery; the practical relevance depends on how soon the next session occurs, which in a community programme is usually the next day
citation: Restoration of Muscle Glycogen and Functional Capacity: Role of Post-Exercise Carbohydrate and Protein Co-Ingestion. Nutrients. 2018; The Effect of Consuming Carbohydrate With and Without Protein on the Rate of Muscle Glycogen Re-synthesis. Sports Med Open. 2021.
ppbf_implication: With 24 hours between PPBF sessions, aggressive post-session refuelling is rarely necessary; a normal mixed meal is sufficient and cheaper.
verified_title: Restoration of Muscle Glycogen and Functional Capacity: Role of Post-Exercise Carbohydrate and Protein Co-Ingestion.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: Food insecurity is documented among collegiate athletes at rates the reviewed literature describes as exceeding those of the general student population, driven by financial demands, time commitments and the energy demands of sport.
study_design: Scoping review of 18 peer-reviewed and grey-literature articles
effect_or_estimate: Elevated prevalence relative to non-athlete students; specific pooled rate not extracted
transfer_status: Transfer to a community youth boxing programme is an inference, not a measured finding
limitations: Collegiate population, not a community youth gym; scoping review including grey literature; self-reported food security instruments; no PPBF-specific data exists
citation: Prevalence of and Contributors to Food Insecurity among College Athletes: A Scoping Review. Nutrients. 2024.
ppbf_implication: Establishes that food insecurity in athletes is a real, published phenomenon; the PPBF-local rate is TBD and would require a validated screening instrument administered with safeguarding review.
verified_title: Prevalence of and Contributors to Food Insecurity among College Athletes: A Scoping Review.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: Elite male and female boxers show a propensity for low body fat; supporting the metabolic demands of a boxing match and recovering between rounds requires a high level of cardiorespiratory fitness, and international boxers show high peak and mean anaerobic power output.
sex: Both, with more data in males
effect_or_estimate: Qualitative physiological profile; no nutrition prescription derived
limitations: Review notes that somatotype studies in boxing are limited; low body fat in elite boxers is an observed correlate of elite status, not evidence that reducing body fat causes improved performance
citation: Chaabene H, et al. Amateur boxing: physical and physiological attributes. Sports Med. 2015.
ppbf_implication: Important framing for PPBF coaches: elite boxers being lean is an association, not a target to impose on a developing athlete.
verified_title: Amateur boxing: physical and physiological attributes.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: A systematic review has characterised the acute physiological, endocrine, biochemical and performance responses associated with amateur boxing.
effect_or_estimate: Characterises acute responses; specific values not extracted
limitations: Acute-response characterisation does not by itself yield nutrition targets; sample sizes across included studies are typically small
citation: Acute physiological, endocrine, biochemical and performance responses associated with amateur boxing: A systematic review. Eur J Sport Sci. 2022.
ppbf_implication: Provides the boxing-specific physiological substrate for round-structure fueling logic; specific intake values remain TBD.
verified_title: Acute physiological, endocrine, biochemical and performance responses associated with amateur boxing: A systematic review with meta-analysis.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: The joint position statement of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, Dietitians of Canada and the American College of Sports Medicine states explicitly that athletes should be referred to a registered dietitian/nutritionist for a personalised nutrition plan, and identifies the Certified Specialist in Sports Dietetics as the credentialed sports nutrition expert in the US and Canada.
effect_or_estimate: No numeric value; the referral boundary is the finding
limitations: Availability of a registered dietitian, and specifically a CSSD, may be limited in a rural community setting; the statement does not solve access, only names the correct role
citation: Thomas DT, Erdman KA, Burke LM. American College of Sports Medicine Joint Position Statement. Nutrition and Athletic Performance. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 2016 (co-published J Acad Nutr Diet 2016).
verification: pubmed:PMID 26891166 and PMID 26920240 (metadata + abstract retrieved; resolved via citation lookup)
ppbf_implication: This is the authoritative basis for PPBF's referral boundary: SHADOW provides frameworks and education; personalised plans are RD/RDN work.
verified_title: American College of Sports Medicine Joint Position Statement. Nutrition and Athletic Performance.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: The IAAF (World Athletics) 2019 consensus on Nutrition for Athletics provides periodised guidance covering pre-event, within-event and between-event eating, and identifies athletes at risk of relative energy deficiency in sport arising from a mismatch between energy intake and exercise energy expenditure.
population: Track and field athletes across event types
effect_or_estimate: Event-specific periodised guidance rather than a single target
transfer_status: Other-sport transfer; the multi-round, multi-day tournament structure of amateur boxing is closest to athletics' heats-and-finals structure
limitations: Athletics events differ substantially from boxing in duration and energy system contribution; the between-event eating structure is the most transferable element
citation: Burke LM, et al. International Association of Athletics Federations Consensus Statement 2019: Nutrition for Athletics. Int J Sport Nutr Exerc Metab. 2019.
ppbf_implication: The heats-and-finals between-event eating structure is the right model for a multi-bout amateur boxing tournament day.
verified_title: International Association of Athletics Federations Consensus Statement 2019: Nutrition for Athletics.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: In a standardised survey of 260 high-calibre Australian competitors across wrestling, boxing, judo and taekwondo using a validated rapid weight loss score, weight-loss practices varied between sports, with variation attributed to competition level and culture.
study_design: Cross-sectional survey using a validated instrument (RWLS)
effect_or_estimate: Sport-level variation in RWLS; specific per-sport scores not extracted
boxing_specific: Partially — boxing is one of four sports surveyed
limitations: Self-report; single country; culture and competition level are confounded; the RWLS is a relative severity index, not a health risk score
citation: Reale R, Slater G, Burke LM. Weight Management Practices of Australian Olympic Combat Sport Athletes. Int J Sports Physiol Perform. 2018.
ppbf_implication: Gym culture is a modifiable determinant of weight-cutting behaviour; this is the lever PPBF actually controls.
verified_title: Weight Management Practices of Australian Olympic Combat Sport Athletes.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: The relationship between weigh-in timing and weight-cutting magnitude is structural: reviews of Olympic combat sports note that official weigh-ins occur anywhere from 3 to 24 hours before competition and that the time available for recovery after weigh-in determines the magnitude and methods of acute body-mass manipulation.
study_design: Two authoritative reviews with a decision-tree framework
effect_or_estimate: Weigh-in-to-competition interval of 3-24 h across Olympic combat sports; magnitude scales with recovery time available
boxing_specific: Partially — Olympic combat sports including boxing
limitations: The causal claim that shortening the recovery window reduces cutting is well-reasoned and consistent with the regain data, but a controlled test of rule change against cutting behaviour was not located
citation: Reale R, Slater G, Burke LM. Acute-Weight-Loss Strategies for Combat Sports and Applications to Olympic Success. Int J Sports Physiol Perform. 2017; Reale R, Slater G, Burke LM. Individualised dietary strategies for Olympic combat sports. Eur J Sport Sci. 2017.
ppbf_implication: Explains why the USA Boxing same-day weigh-in is protective and why PPBF should never advocate for a rule change toward day-before weigh-ins at any level it can influence.
verified_title: Acute-Weight-Loss Strategies for Combat Sports and Applications to Olympic Success.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: Rapid body mass loss in combat athletes affected erythropoiesis and haemolysis without impairing aerobic performance in one study, indicating that haematological disturbance can occur without a detectable performance signal.
effect_or_estimate: Erythropoiesis and haemolysis markers affected; aerobic performance not impaired
boxing_specific: No — combat athletes, sport not boxing-specific in the record
limitations: Single study; biomarker changes without a performance decrement are difficult to interpret clinically; no long-term follow-up
citation: Rapid body mass loss affects erythropoiesis and hemolysis but does not impair aerobic performance in combat athletes. Scand J Med Sci Sports. 2015.
ppbf_implication: Reinforces that 'performance was fine' does not mean 'nothing happened physiologically' - a key PPBF coach-education point.
verified_title: Rapid body mass loss affects erythropoiesis and hemolysis but does not impair aerobic performance in combat athletes.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: The effects of rapid weight loss have been examined separately in male and female wrestlers, indicating that sex-disaggregated analysis of weight-cutting effects is now being undertaken.
effect_or_estimate: Effect estimates not extracted
limitations: Wrestling, not boxing; female combat-sport samples remain small across this literature (156 of 4432 participants in the main systematic review were female)
citation: Effects of Rapid Weight Loss in Male and Female Wrestlers. J Strength Cond Res. 2025.
ppbf_implication: The sex-disaggregated weight-cutting evidence base is thin; PPBF should not assume male-derived findings apply to female boxers.
verified_title: Effects of Rapid Weight Loss in Male and Female Wrestlers.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: Disordered eating risk and mental health concerns have been documented in combat-sport athletes competing under weight categories, with performance pressures and weight categories identified as contributing stressors.
effect_or_estimate: Association between psychological health indicators and disordered eating patterns; effect sizes not extracted
limitations: Single-country cross-sectional design; cross-sectional association cannot establish that weight categories cause disordered eating; taekwondo, not boxing
citation: Mental health, eating disorder risk, and disordered eating patterns among Lebanese National Taekwondo Players: A cross-sectional study. PLoS One. 2025.
ppbf_implication: Disordered eating screening in a weight-category youth programme is a safeguarding and clinical matter; SHADOW may only route, never assess.
verified_title: Mental health, eating disorder risk, and disordered eating patterns among Lebanese National Taekwondo Players: A cross-sectional study.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: Low energy availability is defined by energy availability relative to fat-free mass rather than by energy balance, and this distinction matters because an athlete can be in energy balance while in low energy availability.
effect_or_estimate: Conceptual definition; PPBF should not adopt a numeric threshold, since measuring energy availability requires measured intake, measured exercise energy expenditure and measured fat-free mass
transfer_status: General transfer; the definitional point is universal
limitations: Measuring energy availability accurately in a community setting is impractical: all three inputs carry substantial error, which is why screening questionnaires are used instead and why they are imperfect
citation: Hungry runners - low energy availability in male endurance athletes and its impact on performance and testosterone: mini-review. Eur J Transl Myol. 2023.
ppbf_implication: SHADOW must NOT compute an energy availability value; the inputs are not obtainable to acceptable accuracy at PPBF and a false-precision number would be actively harmful.
verified_title: Hungry runners - low energy availability in male endurance athletes and its impact on performance and testosterone: mini-review.

track: T7-Performance Nutrition
claim: A 2020 updated narrative review synthesised prevalence, risk and within-day energy balance evidence for low energy availability in athletes.
effect_or_estimate: Prevalence and risk synthesis; within-day energy balance introduced as an additional construct
limitations: Narrative rather than systematic; within-day energy balance as a distinct risk construct is less well established than 24-hour energy availability
citation: Logue DM, et al. Low Energy Availability in Athletes 2020: An Updated Narrative Review of Prevalence, Risk, Within-Day Energy Balance, Knowledge, and Impact on Sports Performance. Nutrients. 2020.
ppbf_implication: Supports the case that meal timing across the training day, not just daily totals, belongs in PPBF education.
verified_title: Low Energy Availability in Athletes 2020: An Updated Narrative Review of Prevalence, Risk, Within-Day Energy Balance, Knowledge, and Impact on Sports Performance.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
claim: A boxing performance-analysis template achieved high intra-observer agreement (80-100%) but markedly weaker inter-observer agreement (33-100% across indicators); agreement reached 100% only when a plus-or-minus-one tolerance was applied.
study_design: Instrument development with intra- and inter-observer reliability testing
effect_or_estimate: Intra 80-100% agreement; inter 33-100%; 100% within +/-1
limitations: Small number of analysts; agreement metrics are proportion-of-agreement and sign tests rather than chance-corrected kappa; sample of bouts not stated in the abstract
citation: Thomson E, Lamb K, Nicholas C (2013). The development of a reliable amateur boxing performance analysis template. J Sports Sci.
ppbf_implication: PPBF must report counts with an explicit tolerance band and must never treat a single coder's counts as exact. This is the empirical basis for the A8V-M04 double-coding requirement.
verified_title: The development of a reliable amateur boxing performance analysis template.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
claim: In elite amateur bouts under the Ten Point Must System, winners punched more accurately than losers (33% vs 23% landed; 17% vs 27% air punches), while total punches thrown, defence and interaction time were similar.
population: Elite amateur boxers in a national championship
effect_or_estimate: %Hit 33 vs 23; %Air 17 vs 27; %Hit plus movement index classified 85% of outcomes
limitations: Single championship; male only; the 85% classification describes what judges rewarded, not a causal performance model; correlation is not causation
citation: Human behaviours associated with dominance in elite amateur boxing bouts (2017). PLoS ONE.
ppbf_implication: Accuracy, not volume, is the coachable indicator. PPBF must never display punch volume as a performance figure without its accuracy denominator.
verified_title: Human behaviours associated with dominance in elite amateur boxing bouts: A comparison of winners and losers under the Ten Point Must System.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
claim: Elite male amateur boxing at Olympic semifinal and final level involved an activity rate of about 1.4 actions per second, comprising roughly 20 punches, 2.5 defensive movements and 47 vertical hip movements per minute over three rounds of about 200 seconds.
effect_or_estimate: ~1.4 actions/s; ~20 punches/min; ~2.5 defensive movements/min; ~47 vertical hip movements/min; rounds ~200 s
limitations: Olympic elite males only; the authors themselves note technical discrimination between winners and losers is difficult and outcome may hinge on which punch judges score; pre-2013 rule set
citation: Davis P et al. (2014). The activity profile of elite male amateur boxing. Int J Sports Physiol Perform.
ppbf_implication: This is an external reference point for what elite performance looks like. It is NOT a PPBF target and must never be presented to a youth or novice athlete as one.
verified_title: The activity profile of elite male amateur boxing.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
claim: Comparing elite amateur bouts before and after the 2013 rule change, total punches thrown, rear-hand punches, rear hooks, punches landed, uppercuts and body punches all decreased, while ring movement and defensive movements increased; foot movement rose by a reported 20%.
study_design: Video comparison of 29 Olympic (pre-2013) and 50 World Championship (post-2013) bouts
effect_or_estimate: 20% increase in foot movement; standing counts fell from 9% to 3% of rounds; bouts not lasting full duration rose from 1.7% to 4.2%
limitations: Two different competitions rather than a controlled comparison; male elite only; other factors changed alongside the rules
citation: Davis P et al. (2018). Comparison of amateur boxing before and after the 2013 rules change and the impact on boxers' safety. Br J Sports Med.
ppbf_implication: Rule-set version must be stored with every bout (crosswalk A8-X120). Historical boxing norms are not portable across rule eras.
verified_title: Comparison of amateur boxing before and after the 2013 rules change and the impact on boxers' safety.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
topic: Winning profile in elite women's amateur boxing
claim: In 2023 IBA Women's World Championship finals, winners performed fewer offensive actions than losers but achieved a higher offensive effectiveness ratio across all rounds; pivoting and shifting back followed by counterattack were associated with winning, while parrying and single counterpunches were associated with losing.
study_design: Notational analysis using a customised offensive-defensive interaction cycle framework, coded in Kinovea
sample_size: 12 final bouts; 1323 offensive and 1456 defensive actions
effect_or_estimate: Winners 635 vs losers 688 offensive actions; OER winners 0.39/0.38/0.39 vs losers 0.26/0.28/0.29 by round
limitations: Twelve bouts at one championship; elite female only; winner-loser association is not causal and the finding may reflect what judges rewarded
citation: Notational Analysis of the Final Matches of the 2023 IBA Women's World Boxing Championships (2025). J Funct Morphol Kinesiol.
ppbf_implication: Supplies the OER and DER definitions used in crosswalk items A8-X014 and A8-X015, and directly justifies the counter-after-defence label A8V-D13.
verified_title: Notational Analysis of the Final Matches of the 2023 IBA Women's World Boxing Championships.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
topic: Time-motion phase structure differs by weight category
claim: In 2023 IBA Women's World Championship finals, fighting, punching, clinching, no-fighting and arbitral-interruption phases differed significantly across rounds, and the fighting-to-non-fighting time ratio varied by weight category, with heavyweight categories relying more on clinching.
effect_or_estimate: Significant round differences for punching, clinching, no-fighting and arbitral interruption (all p<0.01)
limitations: One bout per weight category, so category comparisons rest on n=1; elite female only
citation: Time-Motion Analysis of the 2023 Women's World Boxing Championships Finals (2025). Sports (Basel).
ppbf_implication: There is no single correct fighting-to-non-fighting ratio. PPBF must not set a target for this metric; it is a description of style, not quality.
verified_title: Time-Motion Analysis of the 2023 Women's World Boxing Championships Finals.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
claim: Phases of lead and rear straight and hook punches were defined using ground reaction force, EMG, high-speed video and striking dynamometry, producing a shared phase structure for describing punching research.
effect_or_estimate: Phase definitions for four punch types; no accuracy statistic applicable
limitations: Ten participants, laboratory maximal-effort punches, high-speed video; whether phases are resolvable at consumer phone frame rates is untested
citation: Lenetsky S et al. (2020). Defining the Phases of Boxing Punches: A Mixed-Method Approach. J Strength Cond Res.
ppbf_implication: Supplies the punch-phase vocabulary (A8V-B10 to B12). Frame-rate adequacy for PPBF footage is TBD (crosswalk A8-X003).
verified_title: Defining the Phases of Boxing Punches: A Mixed-Method Approach.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
claim: A multimodal system fusing wearable sensor and video data with query-by-committee active learning reported 91.41% accuracy for rear-hand punch classification while reducing labelling effort to about one-sixth of the usual requirement.
effect_or_estimate: 91.41% accuracy at 15% of typical labelling effort
limitations: The paper itself states video-based classification is less accurate than sensor-based due to motion blur; sample and setting not described in the abstract; accuracy is for a research setup, not gym footage from a single phone
citation: An active machine learning framework for automatic boxing punch recognition and classification using upper limb kinematics (2025). PLoS ONE.
ppbf_implication: Automated punch classification is a research capability, not a deployable PPBF feature. Listed as DO_NOT_BUILD_YET (crosswalk A8-X121).
verified_title: An active machine learning framework for automatic boxing punch recognition and classification using upper limb kinematics.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
topic: Automated boxing action recognition - video plus psychological profile
claim: A multimodal deep-learning framework combining 3D-ResNet video features with a BERT-encoded psychological profile reported 91.2% accuracy and 90.9% F1 on boxing action recognition, outperforming video-only and psychology-only baselines.
population: Research video datasets (HMDB51-Boxing subset and a constructed PsyBox-20 dataset)
effect_or_estimate: 91.2% accuracy; 90.9% F1
limitations: Benchmark datasets, not ecological gym footage; the psychological signal came from standardised self-report scales linked to clips, not inferred from images; no external validation
citation: Integrating psychological profiling with deep learning for enhanced boxing action recognition (2026). Sci Rep.
ppbf_implication: Important negative point for PPBF: this paper does NOT show that mental state can be read from video. It shows that self-reported state, supplied separately, improved a classifier. Emotion inference from video remains prohibited (A8V-P08).
verified_title: Integrating psychological profiling with deep learning for enhanced boxing action recognition.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
claim: A transformer approach processing raw video without pose estimation reported 90% accuracy on fencing actions and 83.25% on boxing actions.
population: Research video of fencing and boxing
effect_or_estimate: 83.25% accuracy on boxing actions
limitations: arXiv preprint, not peer reviewed; dataset composition and ecological validity unclear; boxing accuracy is meaningfully below the fencing figure, which is consistent with boxing being the harder problem
citation: FACTS: Fine-Grained Action Classification for Tactical Sports (2024). arXiv preprint (not peer reviewed).
ppbf_implication: Treated as low-authority. Cited to characterise the current state of the art, not to justify building anything.
independent_verification_detail: governing body, statute, regulator or repo document — URL + retrieval date in verification column

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
topic: Pose estimation accuracy in sport - meta-analytic
claim: A systematic review and meta-analysis of markerless motion capture during jumping tasks pooled sagittal-plane RMSE of 5.3 degrees at the hip (95% CI 2.9-7.6), 4.4 at the knee (2.9-5.9) and 4.9 at the ankle (3.9-5.9), with a pooled jump-height bias of -2.9 cm (95% CI -8.1 to 2.3) and heterogeneity from low to substantial.
population: Mixed - laboratory and field jumping tasks
study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis (PRISMA, six databases)
effect_or_estimate: Hip RMSE 5.3 deg; knee 4.4 deg; ankle 4.9 deg; jump height bias -2.9 cm
transfer_status: TRANSFER FROM NON-BOXING TASKS - jumping is a planar, unoccluded, single-person task; boxing is none of those
limitations: Performance varies widely between systems and contexts; wide prediction intervals; the authors advise system-specific evidence
citation: Are we there yet? Systematic review and meta-analysis of validity and reliability of automated markerless motion capture during jumping tasks (2025). J Sports Sci.
ppbf_implication: Even under favourable conditions, markerless angle error is several degrees. PPBF should not present pose-derived joint angles as measurements (crosswalk A8-X122).
verified_title: Are we there yet? A systematic review and meta-analysis of the validity and reliability of automated markerless motion capture systems during jumping tasks.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
topic: Pose estimation in a real competition setting
claim: Testing OpenPose against manual analysis on two-camera 200 Hz footage from a World Championship long jump, coefficients of multiple determination for joint-angle waveforms varied widely and agreement for discrete data was generally poor, with an average ICC across variables of 0.17.
study_design: Concurrent-validity comparison of markerless versus manual digitisation
sample_size: One take-off recording per athlete, men's Long Jump final
effect_or_estimate: Average ICC across variables 0.17; knee-angle CMD ~0.73, hip ~0.37-0.39, ankle ~0.16-0.25
transfer_status: TRANSFER FROM NON-BOXING SPORT - athletics, single unoccluded athlete, two synchronised 200 Hz cameras
limitations: Single event; one movement; a favourable capture setup that still produced poor discrete agreement
citation: Feasibility of OpenPose markerless motion analysis in a real athletics competition (2024). Front Sports Act Living.
ppbf_implication: This is the most directly relevant warning available: pose estimation degraded badly in a real competition with better cameras than PPBF will have. Strong support for the do-not-build-yet position on pose-derived measures.
verified_title: Feasibility of OpenPose markerless motion analysis in a real athletics competition.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
claim: A comparative assessment of 16 monocular 2D and 3D human pose estimation frameworks against synchronised gold-standard motion capture found MeTRAbs best overall, with AlphaPose, rtmlib and YOLOv7 the top 2D performers, evaluated by weighted mean absolute error and weighted ICC on joint angles.
population: Nine individuals performing eight exercises, two camera views
study_design: Benchmark comparison of 16 frameworks against marker-based reference; review of 118 papers
effect_or_estimate: Framework ranking by weighted MAE and weighted ICC
limitations: Exercise videos with a monocular RGB camera, not contact-sport footage; nine participants; no occlusion by a second person
citation: A Comparative Assessment of Accuracy in Video-Based Monocular Human Pose Estimation Frameworks (2026). IEEE Trans Pattern Anal Mach Intell.
ppbf_implication: If PPBF ever pilots pose estimation, framework choice matters and must be recorded per clip. Does not change the do-not-build-yet position for boxing.
verified_title: A Comparative Assessment of Accuracy in Video-Based Monocular Human Pose Estimation Frameworks.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
topic: Head-impact sensors versus video reference in boxing
claim: Across 115 boxing sparring rounds with 5168 video-identified head-contact events, an instrumented mouthguard, skin patch and headgear patch showed sensitivities of 35%, 86% and 78% and specificities of 90%, 76% and 75% respectively, though positive predictive values for head impacts exceeded 96%.
study_design: Prospective validation against three-camera video reference
effect_or_estimate: Sensitivity 35% / 86% / 78%; specificity 90% / 76% / 75%; PPV >96%
limitations: Seven boxers; three cameras used to establish the video reference, which a single gym camera will not match; sensors were also more likely to trigger on impacts near the sensor
citation: Capturing Head Impacts in Boxing: A Video-Based Comparison of Three Wearable Sensors (2023). Ann Biomed Eng.
ppbf_implication: Video, coded by humans with adequate camera coverage, is currently the better-verified way to count head contacts in boxing. It also means a single-camera PPBF setup will undercount. Head-contact counts are exposure records only.
verified_title: Capturing Head Impacts in Boxing: A Video-Based Comparison of Three Wearable Sensors.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
topic: Head-impact sensor signal quality in boxing
claim: Assessing 442 boxing sparring events per sensor, high-quality kinematic traces were obtained in 53% of events for the mouthguard, 20% for the skin patch and 26% for the headgear patch; high-quality recordings were less frequent for impacts near the sensor, and even among carefully selected simultaneous high-quality recordings there was little to no association between the sensors' measurements.
study_design: Prospective signal-quality assessment with pre-defined objective criteria
effect_or_estimate: High-quality traces in 53% / 20% / 26%; Spearman rho >= 0.043 between sensors
limitations: Small participant pool; quality criteria are the authors' own; findings concern kinematic magnitude, not event counting
citation: Quality Issues in Kinematic Traces from Three Head Impact Sensors in Boxing (2024). Ann Biomed Eng.
ppbf_implication: Wearable head-impact magnitudes must not be used for any PPBF individual decision. Counts from different devices are not interchangeable and must never be pooled (crosswalk A8-X049).
verified_title: Quality Issues in Kinematic Traces from Three Head Impact Sensors in Boxing: Prevalence, Effects, and Implications for Exposure Assessment.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
topic: Acute symptoms and head-impact exposure in boxing sparring
claim: Monitoring seven competitive boxers with instrumented mouthguards across sparring sessions, group symptom scores did not differ pre- to post-sparring (median change in total symptom severity -1, p=0.85), symptom scores were lower at 48 hours than pre-session, and no strong association was found between session-specific exposure and symptom change; four of sixteen sessions from three participants showed a symptom-severity change greater than 5.
study_design: Exploratory observational cohort with SCAT5 symptom scale
effect_or_estimate: Median change in TSSS -1 (p=0.85, r=0.07); 48h vs pre p=0.02, r=0.55; 4/16 sessions with change >5
limitations: Seven participants, exploratory and qualitative analysis, no control condition; the authors state the acute dose-response relationship remains elusive
citation: Exploring the link between acute symptom changes and repetitive head impacts in boxing sparring (2026). J Sci Med Sport.
ppbf_implication: There is no defensible sparring-volume or impact-dose threshold PPBF could implement. Sparring volume guidance is TBD and owned by the head coach with medical input, not by SHADOW.
verified_title: Exploring the link between acute symptom changes and repetitive head impacts in boxing sparring.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
claim: A systematic review and meta-analysis of amateur boxing found pooled competition injury incidence of 54.7 per 1000 athlete-exposures (95% CI 33.8-88.4) and 6.8 per 1000 minutes (4.2-10.9), and training incidence of 1.3 per 1000 hours (0.2-7.0); the head and neck were the most commonly injured region in competition (median 72%) and the upper limb in training (median 49%).
study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies
effect_or_estimate: Competition IIR 54.7/1000 AE and 6.8/1000 min; training IIR 1.3/1000 h; head and neck median 72% of competition injuries
limitations: Wide confidence intervals, especially for training incidence; heterogeneous injury definitions; predominantly male samples
citation: Epidemiology of injuries in amateur boxing: A systematic review and meta-analysis (2022). J Sci Med Sport.
ppbf_implication: Justifies both the safety-event branch of the ontology (A8V-J) and the injury-surveillance gap at crosswalk A8-X050. Head and hand are the priority regions.
verified_title: Epidemiology of injuries in amateur boxing: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
topic: Hand injury dominance in elite amateur boxing
claim: In five years of prospective surveillance of the Great Britain amateur boxing squad, hand injuries were the most frequent location overall and in both training and competition; competition total injury rate was 828 per 1000 hours with a hand injury rate of 302 per 1000 hours, and concussion incidence was comparatively low.
effect_or_estimate: Competition total 828 per 1000 h; hand 302 per 1000 h
limitations: Single national squad; per-1000-hour competition rates are high because competition exposure hours are small; medically diagnosed injuries only, so under-reporting of minor complaints is likely
citation: Boxing injury epidemiology in the Great Britain team: a 5-year surveillance study (2015). Br J Sports Med.
ppbf_implication: Supports the wrap-check field (crosswalk A8-X052) and the hand-distress observation label (A8V-J07) as high-prior, low-cost items.
verified_title: Boxing injury epidemiology in the Great Britain team: a 5-year surveillance study of medically diagnosed injury incidence and outcome.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
topic: Perceptual anticipation expertise in combat sports
claim: A meta-analysis of expert versus non-expert perceptual anticipation in combat sports found large effects for response accuracy (1.51; 95% CI 1.15-1.87) and reaction time (-0.91; 95% CI -1.08 to -0.73), with expertise effects more pronounced when the stimulus was closer to the real-world setting.
study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis, seven databases, random-effects
effect_or_estimate: Accuracy SMD 1.51 (1.15-1.87); reaction time SMD -0.91 (-1.08 to -0.73)
boxing_specific: Partially - combat sports broadly, not boxing alone
transfer_status: MIXED COMBAT SPORT - includes non-boxing disciplines
limitations: Expert-novice designs are cross-sectional and cannot establish that training causes the difference; publication bias in expertise research is a known concern
citation: A comparison of perceptual anticipation in combat sports between experts and non-experts: systematic review and meta-analysis (2022). Front Psychol.
ppbf_implication: Supports representative-stimulus design for any PPBF perceptual work, and supports coding decision-related labels as coach judgement rather than measurement. Does NOT license selection use.
verified_title: A comparison of perceptual anticipation in combat sports between experts and non-experts: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
claim: A methodological quality checklist for observational-methodology studies was developed and validated with 54 judges, yielding 16 items across 11 criteria with adequate intercoder reliability coefficients.
study_design: Instrument development with expert judging (Osterlind indexes) and Cohen's kappa intercoder testing
effect_or_estimate: 16 items, 11 criteria; adequate reliability coefficients
limitations: Validated on soccer observational studies; not a sport-performance finding
citation: Chacon-Moscoso S et al. (2019). Methodological quality checklist for studies based on observational methodology (MQCOM). Psicothema.
ppbf_implication: Provides the quality framework the PPBF ontology should be assessed against before any label class is promoted from UNTESTED (crosswalk A8-X117).
verified_title: Methodological quality checklist for studies based on observational methodology (MQCOM).

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
claim: A mixed observational instrument for Olympic taekwondo, combining field formats and category systems across six criteria and 25 categories, achieved optimal generalizability coefficients when applied to 2374 actions from 10 Olympic bouts.
study_design: Instrument design, validation and generalizability analysis
effect_or_estimate: Optimal G coefficients; lag-sequential and polar-coordinate pattern findings
transfer_status: TRANSFER FROM ANOTHER STRIKING COMBAT SPORT - taekwondo is a kicking sport with electronic scoring
limitations: Single Olympic tournament; taekwondo scoring differs fundamentally from boxing; generalizability coefficients reported as 'optimal' without values in the abstract
citation: Design, validation, and testing of an observational tool for technical and tactical analysis in the taekwondo competition at the 2016 Olympic games (2020). Physiol Behav.
ppbf_implication: Demonstrates the design-validate-test sequence PPBF should follow, and shows that six criteria with about 25 categories is a workable instrument size - a useful ceiling check on the A8 starter set.
verified_title: Design, validation, and testing of an observational tool for technical and tactical analysis in the taekwondo competition at the 2016 Olympic games.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
claim: The JUTACTIC judo observation instrument, with 8 fixed and 13 variable criteria, was validated by an 11-expert panel with intra- and inter-observer reliability established via Fleiss kappa and Krippendorff alpha, and generalizability analysis indicated roughly seven matches are needed to characterise a competitor's behaviour.
study_design: Instrument development with expert content validity and generalizability analysis
effect_or_estimate: About seven matches needed for accurate individual behavioural analysis
transfer_status: TRANSFER FROM ANOTHER COMBAT SPORT - judo is a grappling sport
limitations: Grappling sport; small match sample; the seven-match figure is judo-specific and must not be transferred to boxing
citation: Observation system for the technical-tactical analysis of judo by the Rio 2016 Olympic champions (JUTACTIC) (2024). PLoS ONE.
ppbf_implication: The finding that multiple bouts are needed before an individual profile stabilises is the important transferable lesson. How many boxing rounds PPBF needs is TBD.
verified_title: Observation system for the technical-tactical analysis of judo by the Rio 2016 Olympic champions.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
claim: The Coach Feedback Analysis System, with six categories and eighteen feedback types, was developed and validated across 600 minutes of footage from four team sports and multiple competitive levels and age groups, achieving above-acceptable inter- and intra-observer agreement and expert-panel face validity.
population: Coaches in hurling, football, Australian Rules football and women's rugby union
sex: Male teams unless specified; one women's team
sample_size: 600 minutes of footage across four sports
effect_or_estimate: Above-acceptable inter- and intra-observer agreement (values not given in abstract)
transfer_status: TRANSFER FROM TEAM SPORTS - no boxing or combat-sport validation
limitations: Team sports only; specific agreement values not stated in the abstract; coaching contexts differ substantially from a boxing gym floor
citation: Development, validation and reliability of the Coach Feedback Analysis System (2025). J Sports Sci.
ppbf_implication: Offers a ready structure for the coach-feedback capture at crosswalk A8-X020, but it must be treated as untested in boxing and used for coach development only, never for evaluation.
verified_title: Development, validation and reliability of the Coach Feedback Analysis System.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
claim: A handball observational instrument combining automatic and manual variables achieved expert agreement of Cohen's kappa 0.889 and, for two observers analysing a Champions League match, intra-observer reliability of alpha 0.984 / ICC 0.970 / kappa 0.917 for automatic variables and alpha 0.959 / ICC 0.923 / kappa 0.858 for manual variables.
study_design: Instrument design and validation with expert panel and two observers
sample_size: 10 experts; one Champions League match; two observers
effect_or_estimate: Expert kappa 0.889; automatic intra alpha 0.984, ICC 0.970, kappa 0.917; manual intra alpha 0.959, ICC 0.923, kappa 0.858
transfer_status: TRANSFER FROM A TEAM INVASION SPORT - open court, unoccluded players, ball-based events
limitations: One match, two observers with 1.5-2 years experience; handball has a tracked ball and far less mutual occlusion than boxing; automatic variables were higher-agreement than manual ones, which reflects the easier detection problem
citation: Development and Validation of an Observational Game Analysis Tool with Artificial Intelligence for Handball: Handball.ai (2023). Sensors.
ppbf_implication: Shows the target reliability an AI-assisted observational tool can reach in a favourable sport. Boxing should expect lower, which is why the A8 ontology sets differentiated targets by label class.
verified_title: Development and Validation of an Observational Game Analysis Tool with Artificial Intelligence for Handball: Handball.ai.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
claim: Kinovea 2D motion-analysis software was assessed against AutoCAD reference measurements at four camera perspectives (90, 75, 60 and 45 degrees) with three observers making two attempts each, examining both validity and intra- and inter-rater reliability by perspective.
population: Wire-frame lower-limb model in pendular motion
study_design: Concurrent-validity and reliability study against a geometric gold standard
sample_size: One structure, three observers, two attempts, four perspectives
effect_or_estimate: Validity and reliability assessed across four camera perspectives (specific values not in abstract)
transfer_status: TRANSFER FROM A LABORATORY PHANTOM - not a moving human, not a contact sport
limitations: A rigid wire structure, not a boxer; the point of the study is precisely that perspective matters
citation: Puig-Divi A et al. (2019). Validity and reliability of the Kinovea program in obtaining angles and distances using coordinates in 4 perspectives. PLoS ONE.
ppbf_implication: Directly justifies the camera-view field at crosswalk A8-X002 and the A8V-A10 label. Kinovea is the tool the published women's boxing notational analyses used, so it is a realistic PPBF choice.
verified_title: Validity and reliability of the Kinovea program in obtaining angles and distances using coordinates in 4 perspectives.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
claim: For gait joint angles at initial contact in 50 healthy subjects, Kinovea showed intra-rater ICC above 0.85 and inter-rater ICC above 0.90 at hip, knee and ankle, with Bland-Altman disagreement of about plus or minus 5 degrees intra-rater, plus or minus 2.5 degrees inter-rater, and about 2.5 to 5 degrees versus Vicon.
study_design: Reliability and agreement study versus a 3D motion system
effect_or_estimate: Intra ICC >0.85; inter ICC >0.90; agreement approximately +/-2.5 to +/-5 degrees
transfer_status: TRANSFER FROM CLINICAL GAIT ANALYSIS - planar, slow, unoccluded, single person
limitations: Gait is the easiest possible case; boxing involves rapid rotation, occlusion and two bodies
citation: Reliability of Kinovea Software and Agreement with a Three-Dimensional Motion System for Gait Analysis in Healthy Subjects (2020). Sensors.
ppbf_implication: Sets a realistic upper bound: even in ideal conditions, 2D video angle agreement is a few degrees. PPBF should present angles as approximate discussion aids, never as assessments.
verified_title: Reliability of Kinovea(®) Software and Agreement with a Three-Dimensional Motion System for Gait Analysis in Healthy Subjects.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
claim: Pad-based and bag-based boxing-specific protocols of identical structure produced different physiological responses in elite amateur boxers, with higher blood lactate (2.7 vs 2.3 mmol/L), average heart rate (160 vs 150 b/min) and average oxygen consumption (38.00 vs 34.40 ml/kg/min) for pads compared with bag.
effect_or_estimate: BLa 2.7 vs 2.3 mmol/L; HRave 160 vs 150 b/min; VO2ave 38.00 vs 34.40 ml/kg/min
limitations: Fourteen elite male amateurs; single session per modality; findings may not hold for novice or youth athletes
citation: Finlay MJ et al. (2020). Physical Response to Pad- and Bag-Based Boxing-Specific Training Modalities. J Strength Cond Res.
ppbf_implication: Makes the training-modality field (crosswalk A8-X047) mandatory rather than optional. Pooling pad and bag load misrepresents both.
verified_title: Physical Response to Pad- and Bag-Based Boxing-Specific Training Modalities.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
claim: A review of RPE and session-RPE in combat-sport activities reported significant correlations between RPE, blood lactate and heart rate, with a stronger RPE-lactate correlation for official striking matches (r=0.81) than grappling matches (r=0.53), and session-RPE correlating moderately to largely with heart-rate-based training-load methods.
sample_size: Not stated - review of multiple studies
effect_or_estimate: RPE-lactate r=0.81 striking vs r=0.53 grappling; session-RPE vs Edwards TL r=0.58-0.95; vs Banister TRIMP r=0.52-0.86
boxing_specific: Partially - striking combat sports include boxing
limitations: Short narrative review rather than a systematic one; correlation with physiological markers does not make RPE a substitute for them; scale version varies across the underlying studies
citation: Slimani M et al. (2017). Rating of Perceived Exertion for Quantification of Training and Combat Loads During Combat Sport-Specific Activities: A Short Review. J Strength Cond Res.
ppbf_implication: Supports RPE as a feasible PPBF load measure but requires the scale version to be recorded (crosswalk A8-X045). No PPBF load threshold is derivable from this.
verified_title: Rating of Perceived Exertion for Quantification of Training and Combat Loads During Combat Sport-Specific Activities: A Short Review.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
topic: Sparring load changes reaction time and punch force within a session
claim: In seven national-level boxers, rear-straight reaction time lengthened significantly across a 3x3-minute sparring load during the precompetition period (to 390 ms) compared with the competition period (to 310 ms), and both rear and lead straight punch forces were greater at all measurement points during precompetition than competition.
study_design: Repeated-measures within-athlete comparison across two training periods
effect_or_estimate: Rear straight RT 390 ms (precompetition) vs 310 ms (competition) after round 3
limitations: Seven athletes; two training periods differ in many ways beyond sparring load; no control condition
citation: Effects of Sparring Load on Reaction Speed and Punch Force During the Precompetition and Competition Periods in Boxing (2017). J Strength Cond Res.
ppbf_implication: Justifies the fatigue-context field (A8V-K06 and crosswalk A8-X110): a technical label without its within-session position is not interpretable.
verified_title: Effects of Sparring Load on Reaction Speed and Punch Force During the Precompetition and Competition Periods in Boxing.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
topic: Fatigue effects on punching are laterality-dependent
claim: A framework fusing inertial measurement units in the gloves with uniplanar videography and OpenPose in six elite male boxers under a punch fatigue protocol found the dominant side fatigued more than the non-dominant, and tracking simulations showed shoulder abduction and elevation moments increased across the protocol.
study_design: Methods development with statistical parametric mapping and optimal-control tracking simulation
effect_or_estimate: Dominant side fatigued more than non-dominant; increased shoulder abduction and elevation moments
limitations: Six athletes; the authors note the approach would need to move to ecologically valid contexts with multiple IMUs and cameras; OpenPose labelled only left-side upper-limb landmarks in the sagittal plane
citation: Fusing Accelerometry with Videography to Monitor the Effect of Fatigue on Punching Performance in Elite Boxers (2020). Sensors.
ppbf_implication: Laterality asymmetry is real but the evidence base is six athletes in a laboratory protocol. Crosswalk A8-X103 is marked low priority and must not produce an injury-risk output.
verified_title: Fusing Accelerometry with Videography to Monitor the Effect of Fatigue on Punching Performance in Elite Boxers.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
topic: Upper-limb strike force in combat sports
claim: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 28 studies covering nine strike types found straight and reverse punches produced larger mean impact forces than a kung fu punch, a palm strike had lower velocity than reverse, straight or junzuki punches, and the highest recorded mean force was 3427 N for a straight punch.
study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis (Scopus, Web of Science)
effect_or_estimate: Highest mean force 3427 N (straight punch); high-speed strikes over 10 m/s
boxing_specific: Partially - boxing included among several striking disciplines
limitations: Heterogeneous instrumentation across studies makes pooled force values only loosely comparable; predominantly male adult samples
citation: Force and velocity of impact during upper limb strikes in combat sports: a systematic review and meta-analysis (2020). Sports Biomech.
ppbf_implication: Provides an external reference range for punch force but confirms that values from different instruments are not interchangeable (crosswalk A8-X030).
verified_title: Force and velocity of impact during upper limb strikes in combat sports: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
topic: Sport-specific test quality in combat sports
claim: A systematic review of sport-specific performance tests in Olympic combat sports found the majority of studies (74%) had samples under 30, nearly a third insufficiently described participants, 72% did not adequately report inclusion or exclusion criteria, 62% incompletely described or omitted familiarisation, and 60% reported no details on testing-condition stability.
population: Amateur boxing, fencing, judo, karate, taekwondo and wrestling athletes
effect_or_estimate: 74% n<30; 72% inadequate inclusion criteria; 62% inadequate familiarisation; 60% no testing-condition detail
limitations: Assesses reporting quality rather than test performance; findings are about the literature, not about any specific test
citation: Chaabene H et al. (2018). Tests for the Assessment of Sport-Specific Performance in Olympic Combat Sports: A Systematic Review With Practical Recommendations. Front Physiol.
ppbf_implication: The combat-sport testing literature is methodologically weak. PPBF should treat published combat-sport test norms with caution and prioritise its own reliability work (crosswalk A8-X088).
verified_title: Tests for the Assessment of Sport-Specific Performance in Olympic Combat Sports: A Systematic Review With Practical Recommendations.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
topic: Video feedback with learner control improves transfer
claim: Learners given self-control over combined split-screen video feedback and expert modelling during golf-chip practice showed significantly higher form and accuracy scores on a transfer test, higher perceived competence, and recalled more critical task features than a yoked group.
population: Adult learners of a golf chip shot
study_design: Randomised self-control versus yoked motor-learning experiment with retention and transfer tests
effect_or_estimate: Significantly higher form and accuracy on transfer; higher perceived competence
transfer_status: TRANSFER FROM A SELF-PACED CLOSED SKILL - golf chipping has no opponent, no time pressure and no contact
limitations: Small laboratory task; whether learner-controlled review helps in an open, opposed skill like boxing is untested
citation: Self-control over combined video feedback and modeling facilitates motor learning (2016). Hum Mov Sci.
ppbf_implication: Supports building athlete-controlled review (crosswalk A8-X024) but the transfer to boxing is an explicit hypothesis, not an established finding.
verified_title: Self-control over combined video feedback and modeling facilitates motor learning.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
topic: Video feedback plus questioning improves tactical knowledge
claim: Eight expert female volleyball attackers from a national team, split into experimental and control groups, completed eight reflective sessions of clip viewing, self-analysis and joint player-coach analysis; the experimental group showed significant improvement in tactical knowledge measured by verbal-protocol problem representation.
population: Expert female volleyball attackers, Spanish National Team
effect_or_estimate: Significant increase in verbalized conditions and conceptual sophistication in the experimental group
transfer_status: TRANSFER FROM A TEAM SPORT - volleyball, no physical contact, different decision structure
limitations: Four participants per group; expert adult athletes; verbal-protocol outcome rather than on-court performance
citation: An Intervention Based on Video Feedback and Questioning to Improve Tactical Knowledge in Expert Female Volleyball Players (2016). Percept Mot Skills.
ppbf_implication: The three-phase structure (view, self-analyse, joint analysis) is a concrete, low-cost protocol PPBF could pilot. Very small sample, non-boxing, so it is a hypothesis for PPBF.
verified_title: An Intervention Based on Video Feedback and Questioning to Improve Tactical Knowledge in Expert Female Volleyball Players.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
topic: Coach feedback volume and athlete retention
claim: Across 193 young athletes and six coaches, information was completely retained in 31.6% of feedback episodes with a mean per-episode retention of 63%; athletes' practice level, attention during feedback, and the number of different ideas transmitted by the coach were predictive of retention.
study_design: Observational study with content analysis of recorded feedback and athlete interviews
effect_or_estimate: Complete retention in 31.6% of episodes; mean per-episode retention 63%
transfer_status: TRANSFER FROM MIXED YOUTH SPORT - not boxing-specific
limitations: Cross-sectional and correlational; retention measured by recall interview, not by performance change; sport composition not stated in the abstract
citation: Variables affecting athletes' retention of coaches' feedback (2013). Percept Mot Skills.
ppbf_implication: Directly relevant to PPBF's youth population: most of what a coach says is not retained. Supports the athlete recall check at crosswalk A8-X025 and argues for fewer, clearer film-study points per session.
verified_title: Variables affecting athletes' retention of coaches' feedback.

claim: The 6th International Conference on Concussion in Sport produced a consensus statement on sport-related concussion, with a companion paediatric-specific recommendation set derived from the Amsterdam 2023 process.
population: Athletes across sports, including paediatric populations
sample_size: Consensus process, not a single sample
effect_or_estimate: Not applicable - guidance document

citation: Patricios JS et al. (2023). Consensus statement on concussion in sport: the 6th International Conference on Concussion in Sport, Amsterdam 2022. Br J Sports Med.
ppbf_implication: The governing authority for concussion recognition, management and return to play is a qualified clinician. Every A8V-J label and prohibited-label row routes to that human. SHADOW may never make or gate these decisions.
verified_title: Consensus statement on concussion in sport: the 6th International Conference on Concussion in Sport-Amsterdam, October 2022.

effect_or_estimate: Not applicable - guidance document
transfer_status: APPLIES ACROSS SPORTS INCLUDING YOUTH BOXING
limitations: Consensus rather than trial evidence; jurisdiction-specific return-to-learn and return-to-play rules may add requirements
citation: Davis GA et al. (2024). Pediatric Sport-Related Concussion: Recommendations From the Amsterdam Consensus Statement 2023. Pediatrics.
ppbf_implication: PPBF serves minors, so paediatric-specific guidance governs. Named owner for any concussion-related decision is the treating clinician, with the club welfare officer for safeguarding aspects.
verified_title: Pediatric Sport-Related Concussion: Recommendations From the Amsterdam Consensus Statement 2023.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
claim: The American Academy of Pediatrics and the Canadian Paediatric Society oppose boxing as a sport for children and adolescents because it encourages and rewards deliberate blows to the head and face, placing participants at risk of head, face and neck injuries including chronic and fatal neurologic injury.
population: Children and adolescents in North America
effect_or_estimate: Not applicable - position statement
limitations: A position statement, not a study; represents these bodies' judgement, and other bodies and jurisdictions permit and regulate youth boxing rather than opposing it
citation: American Academy of Pediatrics / Canadian Paediatric Society (2011). Policy statement - Boxing participation by children and adolescents. Pediatrics.

verified_title: Policy statement—Boxing participation by children and adolescents.

track: A8 - Video/Film Ontology and Measurement Crosswalk
topic: Boxing scoring authority and video review
claim: USA Boxing technical rules specify a Ten Point Must System in which five judges are seated and three are randomly selected per bout for scoring, with 10 points to the round winner and 9 or fewer down to 6 for the loser; USA Boxing competition rules state that once a decision is determined it is final with no further review, and that personal video recordings are not accepted for USA Boxing competitions.
effect_or_estimate: 10-point must; 5 judges with 3 randomly selected
transfer_status: JURISDICTION-SPECIFIC - USA Boxing only; IBA, World Boxing, England Boxing, Boxing Canada and professional commissions differ

citation: USA Boxing Official Rule Book - Technical Rules (Ten Point Must System; 5 judges, 3 randomly selected).
verification: web_search: USA Boxing technical rules PDF retrieved 2026-08-07

age_range: Any age category per the review scope

topic: Instrumented mouthguard accuracy under direct jaw impact

citation: Accuracy of Instrumented Mouthguards During Direct Jaw Impacts Seen in Boxing (2024). Ann Biomed Eng.

topic: Markerless motion capture in gait - meta-analytic agreement
claim: A systematic review and meta-analysis comparing markerless and marker-based 3D motion capture in gait analysis found good to excellent accuracy for spatiotemporal parameters, moderate to excellent agreement at hip and knee but poor concurrent validity and reliability at the ankle, with pooled ICCs of 0.81 to 0.98 for walking speed, step time and step length.

topic: Wearable punch and plantar pressure sensing distinguishes level
